President Donald Trump said Saturday th...
body_text:
President Donald Trump told reporters Saturday that last month, 25,000 people died in the Ukraine-Russia war and said the month before that 32,000 people died.

President Donald Trump said Saturday that 25,000 people were killed last month and another 32,000 the month before in the war between between Ukraine and Russia

"Last month, 25,000 people died in the Ukraine-Russia war, okay? 25,000," he told reporters on the White House lawn Saturday.

"The month before that, 32,000 people died … mostly soldiers, 97% soldiers. But whether they're soldiers or civilians, think of it: 32,000. Two months ago, 33,000 people; this month, 25,000 people died. What a shame," he added.

PUTIN UNLEASHES NEW FURY ON UKRAINE AS REPORT EXPOSES FEAR HANGING OVER WAR’S END

Russia alone has lost as many as 450,000 soldiers since invading Ukraine in 2022, according to the Center for Strategic & International Studies (CSIS).

U.S. President Donald Trump speaks to the media as he departs the White House on the South Lawn in Washington, DC, US, September 26, 2026. (Annabelle Gordon/Reuters)

Trump also told reporters he wants to see an end to the war soon, revealing he spoke to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently.

KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE

"I spoke to him a lot, and he's going along and Putin's going along. And someday, hopefully in the not too distant future, maybe before the heavy winter, they'll make a deal," he told reporters.

He claimed that he pushed Zelenskyy to try to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

"I agreed with Zelenskyy that we talked about a lot of different subjects, and many of those subjects, very strong agreement. But you know what I want him to do? Make a deal. I want him to settle with Putin, and I want Putin to settle with him.

President Donald Trump greets Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House Aug. 18, 2025 in Washington, D.C. (Alex Wong/Getty Images)

Zelenskyy announced Friday that Trump had agreed to give approval to Ukraine to license and produce U.S. Patriot missile interceptors.

TRUMP SAYS US WILL LET UKRAINE MAKE PATRIOT MISSILES IN MAJOR POLICY SHIFT

"There are concrete agreements regarding Patriot licenses. At our meeting, President Trump stressed that he had made his final decision: Ukraine will receive licenses to produce Patriot missiles,'" Zelenskyy posted Friday.

"There are concrete agreements regarding Patriot licenses," Zelenskyy wrote. (Jens Büttner/Getty Images; Antonio Masiello/Getty Images)

President Trump had previously hesitated to grant Ukraine the licenses.

Fox News Digital contacted the White House for comment.

title: Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair warns Europe ‘we don’t win’ in war without US support
excerpt:
Former British Prime Minister Tony Blair joins ‘Saturday in America’ to discuss the Gaza rebuilding plan, ending the Iran conflict and confronting challenges presented by AI.

Former U.K. Prime Minist...
body_text:
Former British Prime Minister Tony Blair joins ‘Saturday in America’ to discuss the Gaza rebuilding plan, ending the Iran conflict and confronting challenges presented by AI.

Former U.K. Prime Minister Tony Blair warned that Europe could find itself unable to prevail in a conflict with Russia if it loses the backing of the United States, saying British leaders should preserve their alliance with President Donald Trump.

"If we get drawn into a conflict without the support of America, we don't win," Blair told "Saturday in America" host Kayleigh McEnany.

"This is an essential relationship," he continued. "And the reason why I thought we should have supported President Trump when he asked for the use of our bases is in circumstances where your ally is an indispensable part of your security, and they come asking for help, it’s wise to give it to them."

RUBIO QUESTIONS ‘POINT’ OF NATO AFTER ALLIES BLOCKED US FROM USING BASES DURING IRAN CONFLICT

Founding member of the Board of Peace Executive Board and former British Prime Minister Sir Tony Blair speaks at a Board of Peace High Level Briefing on Sept. 23, 2026 in New York City. (Ryan Murphy/Getty Images)

Blair, who served as Britain’s prime minister from 1997 to 2007, called the U.S.-U.K. relationship "an essential" part of the West’s security as European nations debate the threat Russian President Vladimir Putin could pose to NATO countries.

While Blair personally believes Putin poses no real threat to countries outside of Ukraine, he acknowledged that others across Europe hold a different belief.

US INTEL WARNS RUSSIA COULD LAUNCH LIMITED ATTACK ON NATO ALLY IN EFFORT TO FRAGMENT ORGANIZATION: REPORT

President Donald Trump attends the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Sept. 22, 2026. Blair pointed to Britain's alliance with the U.S. as crucial to success should conflict arise. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

"I might be wrong [about Putin]. And there are a lot of people in Europe who think he's got malicious intent towards NATO countries," he said.

Blair's comments come as some European leaders have raised their voices in concern over Russia, including after one recent instance in which an explosives-laden drone was discovered near a Ukrainian cargo plane at an airport in Germany.

A series of other events — including airspace violations, arson and more — have similarly raised eyebrows and pointed toward escalation, per USA Today.

The U.S. and European nations continue to seek ways to bolster Ukraine's defense and deter Russia while refraining from complete involvement in the conflict.

Taylor Penley is an associate editor for Fox News Digital and contributor to FOX Business and Fox Nation who covers media, culture and Flash

title: Someone could have opened an account in your name. Check now
excerpt: Cybercrime losses reached nearly $21 billion last year, prompting Kurt Knutsson to warn of increasingly sophisticated AI scams. He joins 'Fox & Friends Weekend' to break down the FBI data, highlightin...
body_text:
Cybercrime losses reached nearly $21 billion last year, prompting Kurt Knutsson to warn of increasingly sophisticated AI scams. He joins 'Fox & Friends Weekend' to break down the FBI data, highlighting that investment fraud alone cost victims $8.65 billion. Knutsson hosts a free live class to teach families how to protect their money and secure accounts.

Most people think identity theft means someone gets into a bank account or starts charging things to a credit card you already use. But there is another kind of identity theft that can be much harder to spot. A criminal can use your name, Social Security number, birthdate or other personal information to open a brand-new account in your name. And this problem is growing fast. Javelin Strategy & Research found that the number of new-account fraud victims jumped 31% in 2025, rising from 4.2 million to 5.4 million. That was the sharpest increase among the fraud types Javelin tracked.

The fraudulent account could be a credit card sent to an address you have never lived at. It could be a phone or utility account with a company you have never used. Someone could even try to open a buy now, pay later account using your identity. That is what makes this kind of fraud so sneaky. The criminal may never touch an account you already monitor, so there may be no suspicious charge staring back at you from your bank statement. You may find out only when a strange bill arrives, a lender checks your credit, a debt collector calls or you spot an account that clearly does not belong to you. The good news is there are ways to look for those clues before the problem gets even bigger.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Get Better Healthcare With AI replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class Get Better Healthcare With AI has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay now at CyberGuyLive.com

6 IN 10 IDENTITY CRIMES NOW BEGIN WITH A NEW ACCOUNT

New-account fraud can be difficult to detect because criminals may open credit cards, phone accounts or other services without touching accounts victims already monitor. Pasted markdown (Photo Illustration by Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

With fraud on an account you already use, you have a decent chance of spotting it quickly. A strange purchase shows up, your bank sends an alert or your card suddenly stops working. New-account fraud can stay much quieter. A criminal applies for a new account using enough of your personal information to pose as you. If the application goes through, the account may be tied to an address, phone number or email account the criminal controls. As far as the lender or company knows, you opened it. The first clue could be a hard inquiry on your credit report, a new account you do not recognize or mail welcoming you to a service you never signed up for. But there is an important catch. Not every type of account appears on all three credit reports, and some phone, utility or buy now, pay later activity may not appear there. That is why checking your credit reports helps, but it should not be the only thing you watch.

Criminals have more stolen personal information to work with than ever. Years of data breaches have exposed names, Social Security numbers, birthdates, addresses, email addresses and other details that can help someone impersonate you. A criminal may also combine information from multiple breaches, phishing attacks or data broker records to build a much fuller picture of your identity. At the same time, opening financial and other accounts online has become incredibly convenient. You can apply from your couch and sometimes get a decision within minutes. That convenience works in our favor when we are the ones applying. It can also give criminals more opportunities to try stolen identities without ever walking into a bank or store. The Federal Reserve has also warned that digital account openings create new opportunities for fraudsters, especially as stolen personal information and more sophisticated technology become easier for criminals to use.

A criminal may not get everything needed to steal your identity from one breach. Your name and email could come from one leak. An older breach might expose other personal information. A people-search site may help fill in an address or phone number. Put enough pieces together and a criminal may have what they need to start testing your identity against lenders, retailers, phone carriers and other companies. That also helps explain why identity theft can seem to come out of nowhere. The information used against you may have been floating around for months or even years before someone decided to use it.

New-account fraud can leave clues in several places, and some of them are easy to miss if you do not know where to look.

You do not need to wait for a strange bill or collection call to find out something is wrong. A few quick checks can help you spot signs of new-account fraud before it turns into a bigger problem.

Go to AnnualCreditReport.com and review your Equifax, Experian and TransUnion reports. Free reports are currently available weekly, so you can check all three at once or stagger your reviews throughout the year.

Pay close attention to accounts, hard inquiries, addresses and other information you do not recognize. If something looks strange, do not assume it is harmless.

A credit freeze can make it much harder for someone to open a new credit account in your name because lenders generally cannot access your frozen credit report. Freezes are free to place and lift, they do not hurt your credit score and they stay in place until you remove them. You need to contact Equifax, Experian and TransUnion separately to freeze all three files.

Look for messages about accounts you never opened, especially welcome notices, bills, password-reset messages and application updates.

Your bank and credit card companies may offer account alerts at no charge. Identity theft monitoring can go further by watching for certain credit inquiries, new accounts and other signs that someone may be using your information. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at Cyberguy.com . The faster you know something has changed, the faster you can investigate it.

IS YOUR SOCIAL SECURITY NUMBER ON THE DARK WEB?

Identity thieves can use stolen personal information to open new accounts, leaving victims unaware until an unfamiliar bill, credit inquiry or collection notice appears. (Photo by Anna Barclay/Getty Images)

If you spot an account you do not recognize, act quickly. These six steps can help you shut down the fraud, limit the damage and start cleaning up your records.

Call the company's fraud department. Explain that you did not open the account and ask them to close or freeze it. Keep any confirmation they send you.

Go to IdentityTheft.gov and create an FTC Identity Theft Report and recovery plan. That report can also help when you dispute fraudulent information.

A fraud alert tells businesses to take extra steps to verify your identity before opening new credit. An initial fraud alert is free, lasts one year and requires you to contact only one of the three major credit bureaus. That bureau must notify the other two. A credit freeze goes further by restricting access to your credit report. To freeze all three reports, contact each bureau separately.

Contact any credit bureau showing the fraudulent account and ask it to block the identity-theft information from your report. To use the FTC's blocking process, send the bureau a copy of your FTC Identity Theft Report, proof of your identity and a letter identifying the fraudulent information. You can also dispute inaccurate information directly with the credit bureau.

Your bank and credit card companies may offer account alerts at no charge, so turn those on first. Identity theft monitoring can add another layer by watching for certain credit inquiries, newly opened accounts and other signs that someone may be using your personal information. That can be especially helpful with new-account fraud because the criminal may never touch the accounts you already check. See my tips and best picks on Best Identity Theft Protection at CyberGuy.com.

Write down who you contacted, when you contacted them and what they told you. Save letters, emails, case numbers and copies of anything you submit. Those records can save you a lot of frustration if you need to follow up later.

9 WARNING SIGNS OF IDENTITY THEFT YOU SHOULD NEVER IGNORE

Checking all three credit reports can help consumers spot unfamiliar accounts, hard inquiries and other warning signs tied to identity theft. (Photo by: Michael Siluk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

New-account fraud can be especially tough to spot because the criminal may never touch the bank accounts or credit cards you already watch. That is exactly why I want you to check all three of your credit reports instead of waiting for a strange bill or collection call to show up. You can pull your reports for free, look for unfamiliar accounts or inquiries and consider freezing your credit when you are not applying for anything new. Then add alerts or identity monitoring if you want another set of eyes watching for activity you might otherwise miss. The big takeaway here is speed. A fraudulent account that sits unnoticed for months can turn into damaged credit, collections and a much bigger cleanup job. Catch it early and you have a far better chance of shutting it down before things snowball.

When was the last time you checked all three of your credit reports for an account you never opened? Let us know by writing to us at CyberGuy.com.

title: Tenth woman's body found in South Africa suburb as police probe killings
excerpt:
File photo of South African Police Service officers in Johannesburg

Police in South Africa say that they have found a woman's body in a Johannesburg suburb, the tenth in recent months.

The body was ...
body_text:
File photo of South African Police Service officers in Johannesburg

Police in South Africa say that they have found a woman's body in a Johannesburg suburb, the tenth in recent months.

The body was found on Saturday morning and identified by the friend with whom she had been at a bar the previous evening.

The local police commissioner said his force could not rule out the possibility that there was a serial killer on the loose, noting similarities across the 10 deaths in Ekurhuleni, as well as another in Soweto.

The deaths have sparked a national outcry about the scale of violence against women in the country, which has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world.

The latest body was discovered at a cemetery in the Tembisa neighbourhood north-east of central Johannesburg.

Police issued a statement a short while later saying crime scene investigators were at the scene gathering evidence. Officials have yet to publicly identify the victim.

The woman's friend told national broadcaster SABC that she recognised her friend's clothes from the previous night when shown a picture of the body.

"I don't know what I'm going to say to her children," she said while wiping away tears. "It's painful."

Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni said that, at this early stage in the investigation, it was too soon to say whether the woman's death was linked to the others.

He told reporters that the other bodies shared a "similar victimology" that indicated a shared "modus operandi" of killing, which would allow police to determine whether this latest death was linked to the others.

"For now, it's not something which we can overrule to say there's a serial killer, but we cannot conclusively indicate as such," Lt Gen Mthombeni said.

South Africa has one of the highest homicide rates - with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.

But it is the nature of the recent killings around Johannesburg that has left many women there reeling from the growing death toll.

The 10 other bodies have been found in similar circumstances to one another since July. Most of them were found in Kempton Park, one neighbourhood over from Tembisa.

Many of the bodies were those of young women and almost all had suffered extreme violence prior to their deaths.

The deaths have placed pressure on the national government less than a year after ministers declared gender-based violence a national disaster.

While South African police statistics do not differentiate victims by gender, the South African Human Rights Commission said last week that 569 women were killed and 1,052 others survived attempted murder between April and June this year.

Three men appeared in court earlier this week accused of being involved in one of the nine murders, with police working to track down others who may have been involved.

Grim discoveries of murdered women spark fear in South Africa

Ninth woman's body found as South African police investigate string of deaths

title: The wildest things celebrity guest picker Johnny Knoxville said on College Gameday
excerpt: Tennessee Volunteers fans told OutKick's Trey Wallace they're excited for President Donald Trump to attend a key SEC matchup against the Texas Longhorns on Saturday, and they left with their final sco...
body_text:
Tennessee Volunteers fans told OutKick's Trey Wallace they're excited for President Donald Trump to attend a key SEC matchup against the Texas Longhorns on Saturday, and they left with their final score predictions.

It's been quite the scene in Knoxville, Tennessee, Saturday. President Donald Trump is in attendance, the No. 1 team in the country is in town, Holly Rowe and Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian had their first interview since he abruptly ended their interview following their upset win over Ohio State, and Johnny Knoxville was ESPN College Gameday's celebrity guest picker. While dressed in a complete Tennessee Volunteers football uniform, Knoxville made some statements that were just as outrageous as some of his stunts on MTV’s hit show "Jackass."

LANE KIFFIN COULDN'T HELP HIMSELF, TAKES PETTY SHOT AT OLE MISS FANS AFTER LSU LOSS IN HIS RETURN TO OXFORD

Actor and College GameDay guest picker Johnny Knoxville reacts before the game between the Tennessee Volunteers and the Texas Longhorns at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

When choosing the winner of the Missouri and Mississippi State, Knoxville hilariously took aim at McAfee's musical career. "I'm so sure about this game, that if Missouri loses, I will punish myself by listening to Pat McAfee's new album on repeat until Halloween." McAfee busted out a huge laugh immediately with Knoxville saying, "No offense."

ESPN College GameDay analyst Pat McAfee and Nick Saban stand on the lawn of Ayres Hall at the University of Tennessee in Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 26, 2026. (Getty Images)

PAT MCAFEE MIGHT HAVE MADE AN ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION JOKE ON 'COLLEGE GAMEDAY,' LIBERALS LOSE THEIR MINDS

During the Georgia vs Oklahoma selection, Knoxville assigned some pretty gross medical ailments to the respective teams. "You know, I'm from Knoxville so this is like rooting for the gout versus the syphilis. I'm going with the gout. I'll take Georgia," Knoxville stated, while McAfee put his face in his hands and Herbstreit shook his head in disbelief. I hope your kids weren't watching this selection, folks.

LSU head coach Lane Kiffin is the butt of many jokes this season after his rough departure from Ole Miss in the offseason and the loss last Saturday against his former squad so the moment to choose LSU or Texas A&M was primed for Knoxville to lower the boom in his own, special, usually gross way. "I don't know how anyone can root for Lane "Left Out in the Parking Lot" Kiffin. He is to college football what toe fungus is to flip flops. I'm going with A&M."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

LSU Tigers coach Lane Kiffin before a college football game between the LSU Tigers and Mississippi Rebels on Saturday, September 19, 2026 at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, MS. (Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Now it was time for the Volunteers fans to pick the winner of Texas vs Tennessee. After discussing the Tennessee defensive questions, and taking a shot at Texas' offense, Knoxville made his pick. "After the game today, Tennessee will remain the real UT, and Texas will remain the real UTI." The reaction by Rece Davis and Desmond Howard was priceless. Both of them couldn't believe their ears, but it shouldn't have been a shocker after two-plus minutes of unhinged statements.

SEC CROWD GREETS TRUMP WITH MASSIVE CHEERS AHEAD OF TENNESSEE-TEXAS SHOWDOWN

President Donald Trump, Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., and Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., appear on a video screen during the Texas-Tennessee football game at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 26, 2026. Trump, who has attended more college football games than any recent sitting president, watched the matchup between the No. 1 Longhorns and the No. 14 Volunteers. (Getty Images)

Knoxville also jokingly tried slipping a referee a $20 bill pregame during an interview. He was truly a one-of-a-kind, PG-13-rated guest.

Jon is a writer and content creator for OutKick

title: South African police discover body of 10th woman near Johannesburg
excerpt: South African police have discovered the body of another woman east of the country’s commercial capital, Johannesburg, bringing the total number of female bodies found near the city since mid-July to ...
body_text:
South African police have discovered the body of another woman east of the country’s commercial capital, Johannesburg, bringing the total number of female bodies found near the city since mid-July to 10.

Police confirmed the discovery in Thembisa, Ekurhuleni, on Saturday but have not provided any further information. The body was found in the morning, according to the daily newspaper, The Sowetan.

The discovery adds to growing concern over violence against women in a country long plagued by violent crime. While police work to establish whether the killings are connected, there have been community concerns that the murders are being carried out by the same killer or killers.

Provincial police chief Tommy Mthombeni said the latest victim appeared to have been stoned to death, and a post-mortem examination would be conducted to determine the cause of death.

“We have put highly capable investigators on this case,” he told reporters at the scene, pledging to find those responsible for the killings.

President Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged the latest discovery while on the campaign trail for upcoming local elections, broadcaster eNCA reported.

“I’ve sadly heard about 10th body of a woman found in Thembisa,” Ramaphosa said. “This continues to make us very sad, and in many ways, it’s a shame on the men of South Africa that we continue to kill the women of our beautiful country.”

South Africa has one of the highest femicide rates in the world, with an average of 15 women killed per day.

Two women have been charged with the murder of the woman whose body was the ninth discovered, last week. Police have said that the killing may have stemmed from a relationship-related matter.

Mthombeni told state broadcaster SABC that investigators believe the ninth killing was an isolated case. However, he said it is possible some of the other killings are connected.

He added that some of the murders shared similarities, but cautioned that there is no conclusive evidence to suggest the same person or group is responsible.

Police discovered three bodies in July and August within six kilometres (four miles) of one another in Ekurhuleni. Earlier this month, six bodies were found in 10 days, also in Ekurhuleni.

Prior to Saturday’s discovery, all of the deceased women were in their 20s or 30s. Several of them were found completely or partially nude. Police have not yet confirmed the age of the 10th woman or whether she was clothed.

The first body, discovered in mid-July, was found naked. The deceased had been restrained with cable ties. Her boyfriend was subsequently arrested, but no charges were filed.

title: Trump's home county hits pause on data centers over environment and electric bill concerns
excerpt: Resident Artie Carpenter raises concerns over the impact of Ohio's AI data center boom. Reporter Madison Alworth details how surging electricity bills and constant noise are disrupting local communiti...
body_text:
Resident Artie Carpenter raises concerns over the impact of Ohio's AI data center boom. Reporter Madison Alworth details how surging electricity bills and constant noise are disrupting local communities.

Palm Beach County — home to President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago — passed a one-year moratoriam on the planning and construction of data centers as commissioners seek to conduct a thorough review of data centers’ impacts on the environment, noise pollution, and electric bills.

The moratorium, passed on Thursday, comes just weeks after Trump said that communities that reject data centers would "end up being backwards and poor." Among the wealthiest counties in the country, Palm Beach County includes the town of Palm Beach, home to 65 billionaires.

"If you want to go through poverty, crime and squalor, I would say don’t approve of data centers," Trump said from the Oval Office on Sep. 4.

The Palm Beach County Commissioners’ 6-0 vote doesn’t put a permanent ban on data centers. Instead, it gives county leadership time to conduct environmental impact reviews before updating zoning rules for where data centers can be built.

U.S. President Donald Trump holds up a picture of a data center as he holds a cabinet meeting with members of his administration in the Cabinet Room of the White House on August 26, 2025 in Washington, DC. This is the seventh cabinet meeting of Trump's second term. Seated next to President Trump was Secretary of State Marco Rubio. (Chip Somodevilla / Getty Images)

TRUMP’S DATA CENTER PUSH FRACTURES CONGRESS AS LOCAL ANGER EXPLODES: 'GRASPING AT STRAWS'

The moratorium applies to all new applications for data centers with an anticipated peak electrical load of at least 50 megawatts.

"Many communities want the economic benefits a data center brings, but we all fear the higher power bills, the negative environmental impact, disruptive noise, the depletion of water resources," a Palm Beach County resident shared during Thursday’s meeting.

Trump has made expanding data centers and accelerating artificial intelligence a cornerstone of his agenda, arguing that the United States cannot afford to lose the AI race to China and warning that opposition to data centers only benefits Beijing.

Data centers are the physical backbone of artificial intelligence, housing thousands of powerful computers that store and process digital information while providing the computing power needed to train and run AI systems.

Palm Beach County has already approved in 2016 the construction of "Project Tango" — a proposed 202-acre AI data center, which is located 20 miles from Mar-a-Lago. The data center will also be built near an elementary school and homes.

A woman holds signs during a nationwide protest against AI data center expansion outside Peace Hall in New Port Richey, Florida on July 18, 2026. (Thomas Simonetti / AFP / Getty Images)

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS QUESTION WHETHER AI’S PROMISE OUTWEIGHS ITS RISKS

In July, commissioners voted 6-1 to reject a proposal to expand Project Tango by roughly 1.67 million square feet. But existing approvals for two 100,000-square-foot data center buildings remain in place.

Residents at the Thursday meeting said Project Tango was the driving factor behind the push to hit pause on data center project approvals, with several residents advocating for no data centers to be built.

An aerial view of President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago estate, Aug. 10, 2022, in Palm Beach, Fla. (AP Photo/Steve Helber, File)

"I think the best good neighbor data center is no data center," resident Sergei Kelly said. "We have the Everglades to our South and to our West. The coast to our East. I don’t think data centers, especially large data centers they want to build desperately should be here at all."

Fox News Digital reached to the White House and Palm Beach County Commissioners for comment.

Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

title: Belfast court injuncts decision to allow Orange Order march down Garvaghy Road
excerpt:
Andy Burnham calls for calm as fears of unrest grow after request for countermarch in mainly nationalist area

A controversial loyalist parade down a nationalist street in Portadown has been temporari...
body_text:
Andy Burnham calls for calm as fears of unrest grow after request for countermarch in mainly nationalist area

A controversial loyalist parade down a nationalist street in Portadown has been temporarily injuncted after a high court judge urged all sides to “step back from the abyss” and take responsible decisions for “the sake of everyone in Northern Ireland”.

The ruling was made amid rising fears that a parade could unleash fresh sectarian violence.

After a five-hour hearing at a special sitting of the high court, Justice Smyth issued an order temporarily suspending the parade, which was due to take place at 8am on Sunday, until a judicial review application can be fully heard.

She has also suspended the determination by the Parades Commission on Friday that the event could take place, albeit with restrictions on numbers.

However tensions remain with an appeal against her decision by loyalists to be heard at a second special hearing on Saturday night.

Smyth arrived at her conclusions after several attempts to coax the parties, the Loyalist Orange Order and the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition, to reach a voluntary agreement.

After it was clear that was not possible, she said: “The level of mistrust between residents and Portadown Loyalist Lodge cannot be overstated. Neither side accepts any of the reassurances of the other.”

The march down Garvaghy Road has been banned for 28 years due to widespread sectarian violence in 1998 outside Drumcree church.

“It is also clear to me that this particular long-running dispute has the potential to escalate within Northern Ireland,” Smyth said.

The court was sitting on Saturday after a last-minute legal challenge by the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition.

Smyth urged the parties to reach a voluntary agreement to delay the march, given few had time to digest the reasoning behind the commission’s decision.

It was important “to reach an agreement for the sake of everyone in Northern Ireland, not just for your sake” to have the issues “properly aired” so that “everybody knows they’ve had a fair hearing”.

“Be big enough to step back from the abyss,” she told the parties in court.

This followed a high court ruling quashing the restrictions of the annual parade route.

The Portadown loyalist Orange Lodge was not represented at the hearing. But after a request from the judge for its view through the individual who had sought permission for the parade, the lodge made it clear it would not agree to suspending the procession.

The SDLP leader, Claire Hanna, said the parade plan was “provocative”. She told residents she was “so sorry” that some “bad faith actors” were “intent on reopening the hurt and the traumas of the past”.

Fears of clashes increased on Saturday after a request to the commission for permission for a countermarch, a protest that, it was estimated, could be attended by up to 5,000 people, the court heard. That was later revised to 300.

On Friday night, the British prime minister, Andy Burnham, appealed to leaders to “work calmly” through the weekend while the Northern Ireland secretary, Chris Bryant, called for “cool heads”, saying Northern Ireland had “withstood many moments of sharp disagreement over the years” and must do so again.

Before her ruling, Smyth asked the parties in court, including the Police Service of Northern Ireland and the Parades Commission, to “consider carefully the very important issues to our society” raised in this case, and the importance that they were dealt with properly given the “importance of this case to community relations”.

She also noted that the issues of judicial review were of “such fundamental importance” that it could be unwise to hold a full hearing without all the facts.

Democratic Unionist MP Carla Lockhart insisted nationalist residents on the road had “nothing to fear” from the march on Sunday, but Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald described the decision as “utterly reckless”.

The Parades Commission has placed a number of restrictions on the procession, including an 8am start and limiting the number of participants to 35 people, but not placing any restrictions on the route.

title: Nor'easter storm brings coastal flooding, as New York and New Jersey declare emergency
excerpt:
Surf City, New Jersey, was among coastal communities flooded

Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm this weekend, which has already brought coastal...
body_text:
Surf City, New Jersey, was among coastal communities flooded

Tens of millions of people across the north-eastern US are in the path of a powerful storm this weekend, which has already brought coastal flooding, power outages, travel chaos and cancelled stadium events.

Peaking on Saturday, the so-called nor'easter will "bring dangerous coastal flooding and beach conditions, strong winds, and heavy rainfall" to areas including New York City and Boston, the US National Weather Service (NWS) said.

States of emergency have been declared in New York and New Jersey, the latter of which is already facing a coastal deluge in some areas. Rain and strong winds are forecast from Virginia to Maine.

Ed Sheeran's much-awaited Boston concert was among events called off.

Residents on kayaks in a Beach Haven West, New Jersey, neighbourhood

The nor'easter is already causing widespread power outages. Nearly 150,000 households have so far lost electricity, according to poweroutageus.

The Federal Aviation Administration recommended flyers check with airlines about their flight status. More than 1,100 flights have been delayed and another 400 grounded, according to FlightAware.

Saturday's full moon is projected to worsen coastal inundations. Streets and homes were flooded on Saturday in the coastal New Jersey communities of Surf City and Manasquan.

"I urge all New Jerseyans to take this storm seriously, stay alert, and follow local guidance," Governor Mikie Sherrill said.

Flights have been cancelled at Boston Logan International Airport

NWS said in its alert: "Prepare immediately for significant inundation in low-lying areas near the shore, including roads underwater and impacts to homes and businesses."

In New York, officials are warning of wind gusts of up to 55mph (86km/h) throughout the weekend, leading to downed trees and power outages.

"Don't travel if you don't have to," Mayor Zohran Mamdani told residents in a video message. "Do not drive or walk through floodwater."

In the Boston area, the Red Sox moved their weekend series against the Chicago Cubs from Sunday afternoon game to next Friday.

A professional football match between Red Bull New York and St Louis City SC was also cancelled.

Nor is the Global Citizen Festival concert in New York City's Central Park, which was to be headlined by Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and John Legend, going ahead.

Sheeran's concert at the Gillette Stadium in the Boston-area was cancelled for safety reasons, the venue said.

Ed Sheeran's next US concerts cancelled due to storm warning

title: Your favorite grocery and snack items may have disappeared from store shelves in 2026
excerpt: Ramon Laguarta, PepsiCo CEO, addresses the company's Q2 earnings report on 'The Claman Countdown,' detailing strong global snack and beverage volume growth. He notes dissatisfaction with US snack perf...
body_text:
Ramon Laguarta, PepsiCo CEO, addresses the company's Q2 earnings report on 'The Claman Countdown,' detailing strong global snack and beverage volume growth. He notes dissatisfaction with US snack performance, citing plans for affordability investments, portfolio transformation, and away-from-home growth to accelerate market presence.

Shoppers are mourning several grocery store products this year — from a nostalgic juice staple to cult-favorite snack flavors reportedly being cleared from shelves.

Some 2026 grocery exits are confirmed, while others have been reported by food outlets and shoppers.

Coca-Cola confirmed a longtime freezer-aisle exit because of "shifting consumer preferences," The Associated Press (AP) said earlier this year.

DANNON'S DECISION TO KILL BELOVED YOGURT SPARKS FAN REVOLT: 'IT'S WHAT I GOT OUT OF BED FOR'

Meanwhile, PepsiCo announced last year that it planned to reduce nearly 20% of its U.S. product offerings as part of an effort to focus on products with simpler ingredients and functional benefits.

Food outlets have reported that more than 20 snacks could be affected, though PepsiCo has not confirmed every individual product.

Some longtime freezer-aisle and snack and drink favorites spark nostalgia among shoppers. (iStock)

Recently, a list of likely discontinued items across several major brands were featured in Tasting Table.

OLD-SCHOOL SODA WENT FROM BEING A TOP BRAND TO NEARLY UNFINDABLE

Coca-Cola is ending Minute Maid frozen orange juice, lemonade and limeade products, which many shoppers remember fondly from childhood. The company said the move ends its presence in the frozen-can category after 80 years.

"My family would buy these to make frozen icees in the summer," one person wrote in the subreddit r/Millennials. "Can't believe they're being discontinued."

Coca-Cola will be doing away with its Minute Maid brand frozen juice concentrates this year. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)

"This is devastating. Nothing compares. My comfort drink," another said.

COCA-COLA QUIETLY AXED ONE REAGAN-ERA DRINK THAT DISAPPEARED FROM STORE SHELVES

Blue Bell’s Butter Crunch — vanilla ice cream filled with chunks of crunchy chocolate peanut butter candy — is also gone for now. The company’s own product page says the flavor "is no longer available."

"I want them to bring back Butter Crunch so dang bad," one Reddit user wrote in a thread devoted to Blue Bell flavors shoppers want to see return.

The 2026 grocery exits span freezer staples, ice cream flavors and chips. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Cheese Pizza Cheetos Puffs returned in 2025 after a 20-year hiatus, but food outlets have reported that the flavor is now being phased out again.

GEN Z TURNS ON CLASSIC SNACKS, FORCING MAJOR GROCERY SHAKE-UP: 'THEY DON'T TRUST THEM'

The pizza-inspired puffs were among the PepsiCo cuts, Allrecipes reported.

The flavor drew mixed reviews, with some Reddit users saying it did not taste much like pizza, while another said, "I am addicted to these things."

Lay’s Sweet Potato Poppables are another snack reportedly being removed from shelves amid PepsiCo’s broader reductions.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The light, sweet potato-flavored snack no longer appears among the flavors on Lay’s current Poppables page. Reports have said the product is one of several Poppables varieties being discontinued, although PepsiCo has not confirmed.

Food companies are streamlining product lineups as consumer tastes continue to shift. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

"These were such a comfort food of mine," one Reddit user lamented.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Another said his girlfriend's "heart breaks every time she goes to the store because they no longer carry them."

Fans have taken to social media to mourn discontinued and hard-to-find grocery products. (Jeffrey Greenberg/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

While some retailers may still have inventory of Smartfood's Movie Theater Butter Popcorn flavor, fans say the flavor has become harder to find following PepsiCo's cuts.

"Smartfood betrayed me and discontinued their Movie Theater Butter flavor, and I'm a wreck," one Reddit user wrote.

title: Trump rejects combining US-China AI efforts
excerpt:
United States President Donald Trump has said the country will not be heeding growing calls to regulate the development of artificial intelligence.

On Saturday, as he departed the White House, Trump ...
body_text:
United States President Donald Trump has said the country will not be heeding growing calls to regulate the development of artificial intelligence.

On Saturday, as he departed the White House, Trump told reporters the US “is not going to be putting on brakes” for AI, even as US lawmakers and CEOs of some of the nation’s largest tech firms agreed on the need to slow its pace, citing its potential to put humanity at risk.

The president likened those fears to other issues he has previously claimed are “hoaxes”, including climate change and the investigation that examined whether his 2016 campaign colluded with Russian operatives.

“When they wanna put on brakes, it’s just like everybody’s going to be dead. You’re all supposed to be dead now, because of global warming. It’s like Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. All of these different hoaxes,” Trump said.

“What they wanna do is stop our progress, because we’re leading China by a lot,” he added. “And we’re going to keep it that way.”

Trump, who just concluded a 3-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, said the US should not cooperate with China on the technology.

“I would rather not integrate, because we’re leading by a lot,” he said. “When you’re leading, you don’t open it up to each other.”

During his final address before the United Nations General Assembly, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged leaders on Tuesday to enact guardrails on AI, warning that unchecked development “without accountability” could put the world at risk.

US lawmakers and experts had hoped Trump and Xi would use their meeting to deliver a breakthrough agreement on AI. But that did not materialise.

“We didn’t spend that much time talking about it,” Trump said.

As criticism rippled through Washington — and around the world — over the squandered opportunity, the White House on Friday said the US and China agreed to establish a “bilateral communication channel” for AI incidents. There was no immediate comment from Beijing on the White House statement.

The president, however, indicated that any AI discussions he had with Xi, who is set to meet with Trump two more times this year, largely focused on his preferred name for the technology: “super intelligence”.

China “respects” Washington’s switch in phrasing from artificial intelligence to “super intelligence”, the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Saturday, after Donald Trump said Xi appeared to like the rewording.

The US president announced on Tuesday that his administration would rename AI as “super intelligence”, or SI, in official communications.

“Artificial intelligence technologies are continuously developing, all parties can strengthen exchanges, discuss in-depth and seek consensus in light of the latest situation,” said a statement from an unidentified Chinese ministry spokesperson.

When it comes to AI, Xi has taken a more measured tone than Trump and said the technology must develop under human control.

title: Iraq seeks US exemption from ban on Iranian flights
excerpt:
Iraq is in direct talks with Washington as it seeks to exempt some of its airports from United States measures targeting Iranian airline flights in the region.

Four Iraqi airports suspended all fligh...
body_text:
Iraq is in direct talks with Washington as it seeks to exempt some of its airports from United States measures targeting Iranian airline flights in the region.

Four Iraqi airports suspended all flights to and from Iran on Friday, days after Washington announced new aviation sanctions on any global company doing business with Iranian airlines.

The Iraqi prime minister’s office said on Saturday that US exemptions for Baghdad would allow flights to resume “on humanitarian grounds related to medical treatment, education, religious visits, and the interests of civilians”.

The statement by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s media office added that Baghdad was working to de-escalate regional tensions, warning that “the continuation of crises further complicates the situation”.

It called on all parties to pursue dialogue and negotiations to end the current crisis and conflicts in the interests of the region’s countries and peoples.

With Iran flights halted at airports in Baghdad, Najaf, Erbil and Sulaimaniyah, passengers have now been forced onto land journeys of at least 12 hours.

Neighbours Iraq and Iran are both Shia-majority countries, and flights to and from Najaf in particular carry Iraqi Shia Muslim pilgrims to Iran’s holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq.

On Saturday, a large number of demonstrators gathered on the streets of Baghdad in opposition to the flight suspensions, in a protest organised by Iran-allied Iraqi militias.

Dozens of scholars and students from the Hawza of Najaf, the oldest and most influential Shia seminary in the world, held a vigil on Saturday evening against the suspension of Iranian flights to Iraq, Shafaq News reported.

Reading out a statement, the seminary’s Scholarly Assembly condemned the halt of flights, saying it came when “the peoples of the region are most in need of strengthening the bonds of brotherhood”, and urged the government to “maintain the independence and sovereignty of Iraqi decision-making”.

Iraq’s ambassador to Tehran, Yasser al-Hajjaj, said that the suspension of flights between the two countries would be temporary and not affect relations. Speaking to Iraq’s state news agency, he said Baghdad was in contact with Iranian authorities to restore normal air traffic as soon as possible.

Iraqi-Iranian ties are “too deep to be affected by a temporary crisis”, he said, pointing to about 100,000 Iraqi students at Iranian institutions, an Iraqi community of hundreds of thousands living in Iran, and thousands of daily crossings.

Separately, the Iranian ambassador to Iraq, Mohammad Kazem al-Sadegh, said officials from the two countries are in contact and a new decision on flights is likely to be announced soon, Iran’s IRNA news agency reported.

“Iraq is in a difficult situation, allied both to America and to Iran. At times like this, it is squeezed between the two,” said Al Jazeera’s Jack Hewson, reporting from Baghdad.

“Some blame Iran for this, feeling that Iran is too controlling of Iraq. Others blame the US and Israel for having started the war in the first place,” he added.

“Either way, Iraq remains in a very delicate position between all of these larger and more powerful states, continuing to suffer economic consequences and the fallout itself.”

title: German town bans 'stumbling stone' memorials to Nazi victims
excerpt:
"Stumbling stone" memorials - like the one pictured in the Netherlands - are often placed in memory of Jews and other victims of the Holocaust

There has been a wave of criticism in Germany after the ...
body_text:
"Stumbling stone" memorials - like the one pictured in the Netherlands - are often placed in memory of Jews and other victims of the Holocaust

There has been a wave of criticism in Germany after the town of Heidenau, near Dresden in Saxony, decided to ban "stumbling stone" memorials to victims of the Nazis.

Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien told newspaper Bild that the ban was a "scandal".

Since the 1990s, many towns in countries across Europe, including in Germany and Austria, have embedded small brass plaques in the streets in memory of Jews and other victims of Nazi atrocities.

The plaques, called Stolpersteine in German, are often placed outside the houses where the victims used to live or work. They are frequently funded by donations.

But now councillors from the Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) party and the conservative CDU in Heidenau have voted to ban stumbling stones - or "Stolpersteine" in German - in their town.

The AfD in Saxony has been classified as extreme-right by German intelligence, a designation the party rejects.

The motion in the town council said that many citizens felt that this form of commemoration of Nazi victims was inappropriate.

Memorials should in future be placed at the city's Nordfriedhof cemetery to make it "impossible to step directly onto the memorial elements", the motion stated.

Stumbling stones placed near the Reichstag in Berlin

However, Karin Prien, a member of the CDU, criticised the decision.

"Anyone who banishes Stolpersteine and memorial sites commemorating Jewish life from public spaces to the cemetery is prioritising death over life and rendering Jewish people invisible once again," she told Bild.

She said her own CDU party in Saxony also bore responsibility for the decision.

Charlotte Knobloch, a Holocaust survivor and president of the Jewish Community in Munich, said that removing memorials from the cityscape was "completely the wrong approach".

She told the Funke Media Group that she was "appalled that a democratic party would stoop to supporting such a transparent manoeuvre by the extremists of the AfD".

Knobloch said that she was not a supporter of the stumbling stones, but added that "decentralised remembrance – which is not banished from public space but, on the contrary, permeates and shapes it" was crucial to a genuine culture of remembrance.

In her own city of Munich, there are no Stolpersteine on municipal land. Instead, the city allows memorial plaques on public buildings.

As the name suggests, Stolpersteine are intended as memorials people stumble upon, making them reflect on the history of their location.

Gunter Demnig, the artist who initiated the Stolperstein project, said that given the recent electoral successes of the AfD "it was certainly to be expected that something like this would happen".

The AfD recently secured major victories in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

Some branches of the populist AfD are classed as right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence, a designation the party strongly rejects.

Its anti-immigration, "Germany first" and Russian-friendly agenda has found fertile ground in the country's former communist east.

title: US, China strike deal to lower tariffs on $30B in goods after Trump-Xi Washington summit
excerpt: High-stakes discussions on trade and artificial intelligence unfold in New York City as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer meet with Chinese officials. Fox N...
body_text:
High-stakes discussions on trade and artificial intelligence unfold in New York City as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer meet with Chinese officials. Fox News contributor Dan Hoffman analyzes this strategic framework between the world's two most powerful nations ahead of the upcoming summit with President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

The United States and China agreed to lower tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods traded between the two countries following a three-day summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C.

According to the White House, the $30 billion in reciprocal tariff reductions apply to "non-sensitive goods."

U.S. exports including agricultural products, fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices will receive favorable tariff treatment in China. Meanwhile, U.S. imports of Chinese-made small appliances, toys, holiday decorations and children's car seats will also receive preferential treatment.

The agreement was reached through the U.S.-China Board of Trade, a body first proposed during Trump's visit to China in May and formally established during Xi's visit to Washington this week.

President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to speak during a state dinner in the East Room of the White House on Sept. 24, 2026 in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

XI PRAISES US STATE VISIT 'PERFECTION' AS TRUMP CALLS MEETINGS 'VERY PRODUCTIVE'

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC on Friday that "a lot more details" about the new trade agreement will be released on Monday.

Greer said the tariff terms were hammered out after weeks of negotiations. Neither country has released the final tariff rates or all the products that will receive favored status going forward.

This marks one of the most significant cooldowns in the trade war Trump launched against China in February 2025, when he levied a 10% tariff on all Chinese imports, citing Beijing's alleged role in the fentanyl crisis and illegal immigration. China hit back with levies on U.S. coal, liquefied natural gas, crude oil and cars.

President Donald Trump holds up a tariff chart while speaking during a "Make America Wealthy Again" trade announcement event in the Rose Garden at the White House on April 2, 2025 in Washington, D.C. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

BESSENT REVEALS EXTENSION TO BUSAN AGREEMENT WITH CHINA UNTIL JANUARY

At their peak, U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods reached a staggering 145% in April 2025, shortly after Trump unveiled his "Liberation Day" reciprocal tariffs. China responded with tariffs of up to 125% on U.S. goods.

U.S. and Chinese negotiators met in Geneva in May 2025 and agreed to a 90-day truce that lowered U.S. tariffs to 30% and China's to 10%. The agreement was extended for another 90 days in August.

President Donald Trump walks on a red carpet after greeting Chinese President Xi Jinping during an arrival ceremony on Sept. 23, 2026, at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Trump and Xi reached another tentative agreement during talks in South Korea in October 2025. Under the deal, China agreed to crack down on fentanyl precursors, resume purchases of U.S. soybeans and ease restrictions on rare-earth exports, while the United States agreed to further ease tariffs.

The two countries will now use the Board of Trade to negotiate additional tariff reductions and other trade disputes, leaving open the possibility of broader agreements in the months ahead.

James Cirrone is a writer on the Breaking/Trending News team at Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to james.cirrone@fox.com.

title: Craig Carton calls out Pablo Torre for tying Tim Tebow to alleged Life Surge scam: 'Shame on you'
excerpt: Craig Carton goes off on Pablo Torre for dragging Tim Tebow into his latest probe involving Life Surge, a controversial Christian education center under investigation. Carton defends Tebow and warns T...
body_text:
Craig Carton goes off on Pablo Torre for dragging Tim Tebow into his latest probe involving Life Surge, a controversial Christian education center under investigation. Carton defends Tebow and warns Torre:

Craig Carton called out investigative reporter Pablo Torre for his focus on Tim Tebow in a recent report on Life Surge.

Torre alleged that the Christian-focused organization used Tebow as part of a predatory business model that pressured people to hand over thousands of dollars for advice without seeing a return on their investment.

Carton called Torre a "brilliant investigative reporter" but criticized him for linking Tebow to the organization’s alleged conduct without establishing that Tebow knew about it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Tim Tebow is on set before the CFP first-round game between the Miami Hurricanes and Texas A&M Aggies on Dec. 20, 2025, at Kyle Field in College Station, Texas. (David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

"Tim Tebow doesn't deserve to be dragged into this unless you got him nailed. And if you don't have him nailed to the cross on this story, you have defamed him. And if I'm Tim Tebow, I find that to be actionable. I find that to be regrettable," Carton said on a recent episode of OutKick’s "The Craig Carton Show."

Tebow has since come out and said he is "pausing" his relationship with Life Surge.

"I think the allegations are extremely, extremely serious, and it’s something that we take very serious," Tebow told The Gainesville Sun. "And so, for us, we’re having our team do an investigation, but also pausing our relationship until we can learn more about the facts to be able to understand more."

Mother Jones, which collaborated with Torre on the investigation, reported that Tebow spoke at 20 Life Surge events between 2024 and 2025 and was slated to speak at about as many events in 2026. Carton took no issue with Torre’s investigation but lambasted Torre for what the longtime radio host characterized as using Tebow’s name to further his own career.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Pablo Torre and Kevin Clark attend GQ Sports and ESPN's NBA Finals celebration at Artspace at Public Hotel in New York City on June 6, 2024. (Eugene Gologursky/Getty Images for GQ)

"You’re using Tim Tebow’s name and popularity to further your own career. You’re using Tim Tebow to get attention for your story. Whether that story is accurate or not, I’ll take the leap of faith that you’ve reported as an allegation about this Life Surge company that it might even be accurate and factual, and we need to get involved. We need to get district attorneys involved and do a thorough, real investigation to see if they’re committing some type of predatory fraud against honest, God-fearing, blue-collar people who might be losing their life savings under the guise of religion," Carton said.

"That would be awful if that's happening. But how dare you sully the name and reputation of a man who has only done things for others? A man that has dedicated his life to service of his Lord."

Carton criticized Torre for putting Tebow in a bad spot when his reporting did not establish that the Florida Gators legend knew about or participated in the alleged conduct. Carton argued that the report forced Tebow to put out a statement and damaged his public reputation.

"When you go down that road and you sully the reputation of somebody who's dedicated his entire life to service, that is a slippery slope that I want no part of," Carton said.

"So, you better have this locked down, Pablo, and maybe you do, but to throw out an allegation, attach a dude's name to it? Shame on you."

title: California man charged in the killing of his ex-wife – two decades after she vanished
excerpt:
Authorities discovered a body hidden in a home’s crawlspace in 2020, 13 years after Jill Maiorca disappeared

A man was recently charged in California with the killing of his ex-wife six years after h...
body_text:
Authorities discovered a body hidden in a home’s crawlspace in 2020, 13 years after Jill Maiorca disappeared

A man was recently charged in California with the killing of his ex-wife six years after her remains were discovered in a crawlspace beneath a home – and about two decades after when she went missing, according to investigators.

Jeff Maiorca, 53, faces a charge of murder in the death of Jill Maiorca, who was 29 when she was killed, authorities said in discussing what could be one of the latest cases in the US to be solved with modern DNA techniques.

Jill Maiorca’s disappearance was reported in the southern California city of Big Bear Lake in 2007, a statement from the local San Bernardino county sheriff’s department said.

The path to finding Jill Maiorca then began in late October 2020, when San Bernardino sheriff’s deputies received a call to investigate “a suspicious discovery in the crawlspace under [a] residence” in Big Bear Lake. The deputies and members of the Big Bear fire department ultimately located human remains in that crawlspace.

Although the remains couldn’t immediately be identified, an autopsy determined the manner of death in the case was homicide, the San Bernardino sheriff’s office statement said. The agency said its cold homicide case team in 2023 then submitted the unidentified remains for additional investigative DNA analysis.

Such analysis determined the remains were those of Jill Maiorca, according to the sheriff’s office. The sheriff’s office also said that its investigators had come to consider Jeff Maiorca – who had been Jill’s husband and had filed to divorce her in 2004, court records showed – as a suspect.

Citing unspecified evidence, the sheriff’s office’s statement asserted that Jill Maiorca had been murdered in November 2006. Her remains were then concealed – “without the homeowner’s knowledge” – beneath the residence where they were later discovered, the sheriff’s office said.

The agency did not elaborate on the hiding of Jill Maiorca’s body.

Business records reviewed by the Guardian link Jeff Maiorca to a heating, ventilation and air conditioning company. Other records showed his divorce from Jill Maiorca was classified as one involving children.

The San Bernardino sheriff’s office said it arrested Maiorca on Monday. He was formally charged with murder as well as with the use of a deadly weapon, and he had an initial hearing on Wednesday in San Bernardino county superior court, as NBC News first reported.

Jeff Maiorca remained in custody on Saturday at the High Desert jail in Adelanto, California, records indicated. Multiple media outlets reported that he was being held there without bail, and he was tentatively scheduled to appear in court again on 12 October.

title: Scientists reveal surprisingly easy exercise that may boost your mood in just 10 minutes
excerpt: A University of Tsukuba study indicates that running at very slow speed can enhance mood and cognitive function. Dr. Jessica Gray, a family medicine physician, joins 'Fox & Friends First' to discuss t...
body_text:
A University of Tsukuba study indicates that running at very slow speed can enhance mood and cognitive function. Dr. Jessica Gray, a family medicine physician, joins 'Fox & Friends First' to discuss the details.

It might not take an all-out sprint or long trail run to lift your mood and sharpen focus, according to a new study.

A small new study out of the University of Tsukuba in Japan looked at 24 healthy young adults who completed a slow, 10-minute run on the treadmill in one session and rested in another.

After the easy jog, participants performed faster on a test of attention and self-control and reported feeling more alert and pleasant than they did after the resting phase, according to the study, which was published in the journal Imaging Neuroscience in August.

'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS

Brain monitoring after the jog also showed more activity in parts of the prefrontal cortex, the area of the brain responsible for focus and decision-making.

A small study suggests even a brief, easy jog may offer a short-term boost in mood and focus. (iStock)

The jog was purposely kept easy, with participants going at speeds from 1.9 to 3.7 mph on the treadmill. Their average heart rates clocked in at 105 to 107 beats per minute.

SIMPLE BODY MOVEMENT COULD HELP THE BRAIN 'CLEAN ITSELF,' RESEARCHERS FIND

"A single bout of running, even at very slow speed, elicits a pleasant mood and improved executive function," the researchers found.

They added that the finding "sheds light on the slow running benefits to brain health."

Even gentle movement can provide a mental reset, though the study’s findings were limited to one short session. (iStock)

JUST 10 MINUTES OF DAILY FLOOR EXERCISES MAY IMPROVE BALANCE AND AGILITY, STUDY FINDS

The benefits, they noted, stuck around even after participants' heart rates returned to baseline.

The greater the up-and-down head movement during the jog, the more positive participants' mood was afterward, though that finding was exploratory and does not necessarily prove cause and effect.

5 COMMON WALKING MISTAKES THAT COULD HURT YOUR PROGRESS, ACCORDING TO AN EXPERT

"Easy movement triggers the norepinephrine and dopamine pathways that wake up the part of the brain that is in charge of focus and self-control," explained Dr. John La Puma, a California-based internist and author of "Indoor Epidemic," who was not involved in the study.

Brain monitoring during the post-jog attention test showed greater activity in prefrontal regions involved in focus and decision-making. (iStock)

Experts agree, however, that it does not mean one brief workout could be a cure-all.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"A brief jog should help someone get some energy in their system, which may make them feel better about themselves mentally and help them focus," said Dr. Scott Nass, a California-based family medicine physician at SwiftCareMD.

But Nass, who also wasn't involved in the research, said that the effect is likely temporary.

Participants completed a test measuring attention and self-control after a 10-minute easy jog and after a resting session. (iStock)

For people living with depression or anxiety, a jog may briefly clear the mind but is "no substitute for medical care," he told Fox News Digital.

The study was also limited in that it included just 24 healthy, young adults and measured outcomes immediately after just one exercise session. The findings cannot be assumed to apply to older adults, novice runners or people with health conditions and larger studies are needed to confirm the results, Nass said.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For a practical approach, La Puma suggested taking a 10-minute walk outside before the most mentally demanding part of the day. Add 30-second jogging intervals, keeping the pace easy enough to speak in full sentences without becoming breathless, he said.

After the slow jog, participants reported feeling more alert and pleasant than they did following the resting session. (iStock)

People with heart disease, high blood pressure, Type 1 diabetes, recent surgery or joint pain should check with a clinician before starting a new routine, La Puma advised.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the researchers for comment.

Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

title: One year on, the UK’s recognition of Palestinian statehood is bearing fruit
excerpt:
Ambassador of the State of Palestine to the United Kingdom.

This week marks one year since the United Kingdom, along with nine other Western countries, recognised the State of Palestine. What shifted...
body_text:
Ambassador of the State of Palestine to the United Kingdom.

This week marks one year since the United Kingdom, along with nine other Western countries, recognised the State of Palestine. What shifted was politics, not policy: overwhelming support for the Palestinian cause by the British public finally persuaded the government to align with the law.

For decades, the UK backed a two-state solution in words only. Its logic was twisted: recognise statehood only after a final peace agreement, handing Israel a veto over the very policy it claimed to support, even as successive Israeli governments worked – through words, bulldozers and bombs – to render Palestinian statehood impossible.

This approach treated Palestinian self-determination as conditional, not an inalienable right — earned through reform, “good governance” and benchmarks no other people have been made to meet.

The British recognition of Palestinian statehood marked a turning point – one that is already bearing fruit a year later. Upgrading relations with Palestine has allowed the UK to turn rhetoric into policy.

Almost a year after the UK formally recognised the State of Palestine, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced that the British government now regards the Israeli occupation of Palestinian lands as unlawful.

He then set out bans on settlement goods, services, advertising and arms licences, as well as sanctions on companies that build, finance or sell settlement homes. This move is a logical next step after the British recognition of Palestinian statehood.

The British foreign secretary, to his credit, acknowledged Britain should have acted sooner. Prime Minister Andy Burnham put it plainly: support for two states is “meaningless unless we back it up with action”.

The legal groundwork for these measures was laid in July 2024, when the International Court of Justice declared Israel’s occupation unlawful, along with the separation wall and settlements, and its near-total separation of settlers to be equivalent to racial segregation and apartheid. The court ruled the occupation must end “as rapidly as possible”.

After Miliband’s announcement, 11 other governments, including Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, ⁠Poland, Portugal, Spain, and ⁠Sweden, joined a parallel statement on sanctions and trade with settlements.

These measures matter because the occupation runs on an ecosystem of contractors, lenders, estate agents and Israeli state institutions sponsoring the settlements — and the new rules must reach every part of it. For decades, words on Palestine cost nothing while settlements multiplied; now there are consequences.

Israel has responded. It has ordered London to close its consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, which it cannot legally do since it holds no sovereignty there. The punitive measures unleashed onto the Palestinian population are worse still.

Since September 2, Israeli forces have demolished every home in Khirbet al-Tabban and northern al-Fakhit in the occupied West Bank, leaving roughly 70 people, 28 of them children, without shelter.

Settlement activities have also accelerated. Earlier this month, the occupation authorities issued tenders for 3,401 planned housing units as part of the E1 project, which would cut off occupied East Jerusalem from the occupied West Bank.

In Gaza, where two million of our people are confined to less than 30 percent of the Strip’s territory, Israel continues to bomb and kill civilians. More than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called ceasefire began last October last year. Meanwhile, more than 140,000 tarpaulins and 7,500 tents meant to provide shelter for the winter for homeless Palestinians sit blocked in the Jordan corridor.

For too long, countries like the UK exercised caution and hesitation, sending the wrong signal to Israel, inviting more aggressive action and solidifying its culture of impunity.

For that to change, the announced sanction measures need to be followed by action.

First, there needs to be immediate and full implementation. The sanctions must be put into practice and the 12 governments should agree on how they will respond to pressure to reverse course. Unity can help withstand coercion.

Second, there needs to be protection for the people these measures exist for. The olive harvest begins next month in Palestine. During last year’s harvest, the United Nations recorded 126 settler attacks in 70 towns and villages within its first three weeks. This year’s harvest is the first real test of whether settler sanctions carry weight on the ground.

Collective action should not be limited to the occupied West Bank. There must be efforts to end the ongoing genocide in Gaza and Israel’s continuing violations of the ceasefire. Urgently, there needs to be pressure to secure the delivery of aid, particularly the much-needed shelter materials held in the Jordan corridor.

Moving forward, we must remember the example of apartheid South Africa. The boycott and sanctions campaign was resisted by Western governments, including the British one, and their action is remembered now as lagging behind their people.

This time, the UK can lead and be judged differently, if it holds its nerve, moving together with a growing number of partners, as it did with the 11 other governments two weeks ago.

Next year marks 110 years since the Balfour Declaration, 80 since the UN partition vote, and 60 since the occupation began. Palestine has had enough beginnings. What it needs now is an ending.

For the first time in a generation, law, politics and sentiment in London are beginning to point the same way. This is Britain’s chance to lead a better future and redeem the past.

When the occupation ends, and it will, the path to a peace rooted in justice, dignity and equality can finally be laid.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

title: 'Mike & Molly' star Billy Gardell admits weight loss surgery 'probably saved' his life

Ethan Suplee reflects on the ongoing responsibility that comes with becoming a public weight-loss success story and explains why consistent support from like-minded people keeps him on track.

"Mike & Molly" star Billy Gardell is sharing how his dramatic weight loss following his bariatric surgery in 2021 has changed his life.

During a recent appearance on the "Breaking Bread" podcast, the 57-year-old actor said his decision to undergo the surgery "probably saved my life" and described the circumstances which led to him deciding that was the right route for him.

He explained that he had developed type 2 diabetes, as well as "some cholesterol stuff, some heart stuff," joking that his doctor told him that "after 50 the warranties start running out."

"You can't outrun those. I think the only reason I was able to survive as long as I did is one, I got decent genetics, and two was I played some sports when I was younger. So I was a big fat guy, but I was a pretty solid fat guy, and I could carry the weight for a long time, but eventually you can't outrun that."

Gardell credits his weight loss surgery for saving his life. (Getty Images)

'REMEMBER THE TITANS' STAR ETHAN SUPLEE SAYS ONE HARD TRUTH FUELED HIS 300-POUND WEIGHT LOSS

After a certain point, Gardell said his doctor approached him and said, "You have to do something."

"I got to the point where I hurt my knee and I couldn't even walk for exercise, and I was like, I have to do something drastic," he said. "So I got the surgery, and it's been a couple years now and I probably saved my life. I'm not on any medication. Diabetes is gone."

Five years after the surgery, the actor explained he has "to be real selective" about what he eats, because he only has "12 ounces to work with," but said the issue with that is "the fat Hulk is still running around" in his mind wanting to overindulge.

Aside from saving his life, the surgery and resulting weight loss also allowed him to do things he couldn't do before, including hiking with his wife and buying something "off the rack" when shopping at the mall.

Gardell is enjoying the little things in life since losing weight. (Michael Simon/Getty Images)

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"It's just those little freedoms that you go, 'Wow, man. I'm so grateful I can do this now,'" he said. "I know those are simple, stupid things, but they mean the world to me."

Gardell explained he decided to get healthy not only for himself, but also for his wife, Patty Knight and their son, William, calling them "my motivating factors."

"It was like I don't want to survive what I've survived, succeed where I succeeded, and then not be able to get out of a chair. So I had to look that in its face. And for anybody out there struggling, if I can do it, you can do it. And don't let nobody tell you different. Do whatever it takes."

Throughout his life, Gardell said he would often fluctuate, losing and gaining 30 pounds every year, noting at his heaviest, he weighed 379 pounds.

Gardell starred alongside McCarthy on "Mike & Molly" for six years. (Sonja Flemming/CBS via Getty Images)
