title: Turkiye vs France: UEFA Nations League – teams, kickoff time, lineups
excerpt:
Who: Turkiye vs France
What: UEFA Nations League
Where: Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, Turkiye
When: Friday, September 25, at 9:45pm (18:45 GMT)
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up f...
body_text:
Who: Turkiye vs France
What: UEFA Nations League
Where: Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, Turkiye
When: Friday, September 25, at 9:45pm (18:45 GMT)
How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will have all the build-up from 15:45 GMT.

Zinedine Zidane was asked if taking charge of his first France game on Friday will feel just as special as his playing debut for Les Bleus more than 30 years ago.

“Even more so, maybe,” a smiling Zidane said on Thursday ahead of a Nations League game in Turkiye. “I feel an immense emotion being at the head of this France team.”

Zidane’s dream was realised when he replaced Didier Deschamps after the 2026 World Cup. His former teammate Deschamps was in charge for 14 years, winning the World Cup in 2018 and losing the 2022 final.

Now it’s Zidane’s chance to make his mark on a team he once starred for.

Affectionately nicknamed “Zizou”, his face was beamed onto the Arc de Triomphe in Paris the night France celebrated its first World Cup triumph in 1998.

Zidane scored two headers in the final in a 3-0 win over Brazil and later that year he won the Ballon d’Or. Two years later, he was instrumental in France winning the European Championship.

His rise to the top seemed almost fated, for his international career began brilliantly in 1994 with two stunning goals against the Czech Republic after coming on as a substitute.

He then won league titles with Juventus and Real Madrid and scored a brilliant volley to help Madrid win the Champions League in 2002.

Zidane understands expectations are high, given his achievements as a player and how he led Real Madrid to three straight Champions League titles as a coach.

“It’s something new. I’m taking over as head coach so people are talking about it,” he said. “That makes sense.”

After facing Turkiye, France plays Belgium away on Monday before hosting Italy on October 2, and Belgium three days later, with both those games at the Stade de France.

France’s all-time top scorer Kylian Mbappe is set to captain the side, having shrugged off a minor injury.

Zidane was asked why, given that Mbappe is captain, he was not present at Thursday’s pre-match news conference. Instead, it was midfielder Adrien Rabiot who spoke to the media.

“The obligation is to have one player and the coach,” Zidane said. “[Mbappe] is fine. He will be ready to play tomorrow.”

Rabiot is one of France’s vice-captains along with forward Ousmane Dembele and right back Jules Kounde.

Rabiot said the huge attention placed on Zidane gave the players a welcome back seat.

“His aura means he commands a lot of attention,” Rabiot said. “In a way, it’s a good thing that the focus is more on the coach than the players. It gives them a bit more peace and quiet.”

Zidane understands the limelight but does not seek it.

“You have to accept how things are. But I’m not here for that,” he said. “Winning matches is what interests me the most.”

The sides shared a 1-1 draw in Paris in 2019 in a qualifier for Euro 2020.

Olivier Giroud gave the home side the lead in the 76th minute before Kaan Ayhan levelled for Turkiye five minutes later.

This will be the seventh meeting between the nations, with France claiming four wins to Turkiye’s one in the previous encounters.

Turkiye will be without the services of Hakan Calhanoglu and Kenan Yildiz due to injury. Real Madrid starlet Arda Guler, however, is available despite fears of a knock.

Cakir; Celik, Demiral, Bardakci, Elmali; Ozcan, Kokcu, Yuksek; Guler, Yilmaz, Akturkoglu

Zidane can choose from six new faces in his squad.

Striker Esteban Lepaul (Rennes), defenders Leny Yoro (Manchester United) and Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool), midfielder Lucas Da Cunha (Como), Andy Diouf (Inter Milan) and Guillaume Restes (Toulouse) are set for their debuts.

“I’m happy with what I’ve seen so far. The French team is open to everyone,” Zidane said. “We’ve got a good squad, some veterans, some newcomers.”

Maignan; Kounde, Upamecano, Lacroix, Truffert; Camavinga, Rabiot; Dembele, Olise, Doue; Mbappe

title: AOC's 'Tax the Rich' designer accused of leaving small business with massive charity gala bill
excerpt: 'Outnumbered' reacts slam self-described progressive Grace Ryan, dubbed 'Lulu Lenin.' The wealthy socialist defended her privilege on social media by citing 'noblesse oblige.' The panel criticizes the...
body_text:
'Outnumbered' reacts slam self-described progressive Grace Ryan, dubbed 'Lulu Lenin.' The wealthy socialist defended her privilege on social media by citing 'noblesse oblige.' The panel criticizes the hypocrisy of wealthy progressives who advocate for policies that harm communities while relying on personal safety nets.

The fashion designer behind Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's, D-N.Y., "Tax the Rich" Met Gala dress is facing a seven-figure lawsuit accusing her of stiffing the small business she hired to throw her own star-studded charity gala.

According to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital, designer Aurora James, 42, is being sued by event organizer The Gathery Inc. over allegations stemming from unpaid bills after it produced the "15 Percent Pledge Gala 2026″ at Paramount Studios in Los Angeles earlier this year.

The February bash boasted an attendee list that included Meghan Markle and Kimora Lee Simmons, and was held with the intention of raising money for Black business owners.

ANNA WINTOUR REPORTEDLY FACES CALLS TO RETIRE AFTER JOHN GALLIANO MET GALA FIRESTORM: ‘LOST HER TOUCH’

Aurora James and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., attend the 2021 Met Gala celebrating In America: A Lexicon of Fashion at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City on Sept. 13, 2021. (Getty Images)

However, a civil lawsuit filed in New York Supreme Court by The Gathery alleges James, her nonprofit 15 Percent Pledge, and its fiscal sponsor, Philanthropic Ventures Foundation (PVF) left the planners with the bill.

The plaintiffs are seeking at least $1,082,965.28 in damages from the three parties, along with contractually owed interest and additional financial damages.

According to court documents, James’s nonprofit allegedly made two initial deposits toward the $1.5 million bill to The Gathery — which produced the annual fundraiser in both 2024 and 2025 without issue — before ceasing all payments in November 2025.

James "personally directed the project and repeatedly induced TGI to continue performing even after payment defaults had begun," the suit reads.

PRINCE HARRY SUED BY CHARITY HE FOUNDED IN HONOR OF PRINCESS DIANA

Aurora James attends the Altuzarra fashion show during New York Fashion Week: The Shows at the Woolworth Building on Sept. 12, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)

"James approved change orders expanding the scope and cost of the event, signed the Feb. 4, 2026, amendment admitting breach, and assured TGI that payment would be forthcoming — all while knowing, or recklessly disregarding, that 15PP lacked the ability to pay," it continued.

James founded the nonprofit organization in 2020 in response to the murder of George Floyd, with a goal of encouraging retailers to dedicate 15% of their storefront’s shelf space to products created by Black-owned businesses.

According to its website, 15 Percent Pledge is a self-described "racial equity and economic justice non-profit organization working towards a more equitable economic future."

"Launched in 2020 by Aurora James, the initiative was born from seeing multiple acts of injustice and police brutality in the United States with a lack of accountability for the systemic issues at play," the website states.

DEFEATED PROGRESSIVE ‘SQUAD’ LAWMAKER IN HOT SEAT FOR NON-PROFIT’S MISSING PAPER TRAIL

Canadian fashion designer Aurora James arrives for the 2026 Met Gala celebrating "Costume Art" at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York on May 4, 2026. (AFP via Getty Images)

The ongoing civil lawsuit is not James’ first time allegedly missing payments.

James, who shares a son with Benjamin Bronfman — son of music executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. and actress Sherry Brewer — was reported in 2021 to have run up tax debts through Cultural Brokerage Agency, the parent company of her Brother Vellies fashion brand, including three open state tax warrants from 2018-19 totaling $14,798 in unpaid employee withholding and 15 warrants since 2015, according to The New York Post.

The company has also reportedly faced multiple legal claims alleging it repeatedly failed to pay worker benefits.

The alleged financial hypocrisy by James — an outspoken activist with deep ties to the fashion world — was noted by both legal and political experts.

"These are still allegations that have to be proven in court, but there’s an undeniable irony in an organization dedicated to supporting small businesses being accused of stiffing one for more than $1 million," former Palm Beach County State Attorney Dave Aronberg told Fox News Digital. "If you preach economic fairness, you have to practice it too."

AOC DOUBLES DOWN ON ‘MYTH’ OF EARNING A BILLION DOLLARS, CLAIMS FORTUNES ARE BUILT ON ‘ABUSE’

Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez wore a dress that said "Tax the Rich" to the 2021 Met Gala, a popular sentiment among those on the left.  (Kevin Mazur/MG21/Getty Images For The Met Museum/Vogue)

Kaivon Shroff, a former digital organizer for Hillary Clinton’s campaign, also noted the apparent irony in the allegations against James.

"AOC made Aurora James’s ‘Tax the Rich’ dress one of the defining political images of the Met Gala and excess wealth at a time of great economic inequality, so the irony here is impossible to miss," Shroff told Fox News Digital.

"James built her public brand around economic justice and supporting Black-owned businesses," he added, while noting that now she is being sued by a small business.

"That is exactly the kind of contradiction opponents seize on to argue that the politics are performative," Shroff said.

"Movements built around economic fairness and supporting marginalized businesses are so important, and they depend heavily on credibility and goodwill," he added. "When the people most visibly associated with those causes are accused of behaving in ways that seem completely at odds with the message, the damage does not stop with the individual. It gives critics an easy way to discredit the cause itself."

Fox News Digital reached out to James’ attorney for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Julia Bonavita is a media and culture writer for Fox News Digital, and a Fox Flight Team drone pilot. You can follow her at @juliabonavita13 on all platforms and send story tips to julia.bonavita@fox.com.

title: Australia news live: Paterson says PM’s AI hack timing not a coincidence; gen Z going without for a house
excerpt:

The opposition’s defence spokesperson, James Paterson, has questioned the timing of the prime minister’s announcement that an AI agent hack...
body_text:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The opposition’s defence spokesperson, James Paterson, has questioned the timing of the prime minister’s announcement that an AI agent hacked Medicare.

Paterson made the claim on the ABC’s 7.30 program last night after Anthony Albanese publicly disclosed that an AI agent developed by OpenAI hacked Medicare in June and that the tech giant only notified the government earlier this month using an email sent to a “public mailbox”.

Paterson told 7.30 he believed Albanese had chosen to make the announcement at the UN summit in New York, as part of his effort to stand up to “big tech” on AI.

double quotation markThe government has questions to answer about when they knew and … why the prime minister decided to disclose it in the way he did in the place he did at the time he did. But in terms of the nature of the potential of actual security breach this is the bottom end of the spectrum of seriousness.

I don’t think it was a coincidence. I think it neatly dove-tailed with the political agenda the prime minister has in New York City.

Paterson said he didn’t consider the breach to be overly serious because the data the AI agent accessed was made freely available to researchers and academics studying the health system, and was not personal or private in nature.

He said the breach was cause for “being alert but not alarmed”.

Nevertheless, he said Australians were “entitled to demand explanations and contrition” and to want high levels of confidence when entering into agreements with big tech companies such as OpenAI.

Charlton says AI incidents likely to become ‘more and more prevalent’

Andrew Charlton, the assistant minister for science, technology and the digital economy, said yesterday’s reported hack of Medicare by an OpenAI agent was a “novel” moment for cybersecurity, but was likely to become “more and more prevalent in the future”.

Charlton spoke to RN Breakfast this morning, saying the government wanted to tell the Australian public “as quickly as possible” about the breach. When pressed why it took Services Australia five days to notify the Australian Signals Directorate about the episode, Charlton said the true blame laid on OpenAI’s slow and “completely inadequate” response:

double quotation markIn this type of situation, you know, you would expect for an incident which is as serious as this, you would expect that disclosure to be delivered in a very serious way. It was not delivered in a very serious way, it was delivered via an email to a public inbox.

He said the government is still looking at any legal action and there were questions about liability as an AI agent was “not a legal person”.

Falling meth prices help drive deaths to record levels

Falling methamphetamine prices have helped push overdose deaths to record levels, new data shows.

AAP reports increased global supply and strong local demand are among the factors driving a surge in use of the illicit drug, according to the National Drug and Alcohol Research Centre.

“Use and harms remain substantial and appear to have continued the upward trajectory that we saw before the Covid-19 pandemic,” University of NSW Sydney medical researcher Amy Peacock told AAP.

double quotation markIn fact, several of the indicators are now at the highest observed levels that we’ve seen, including wastewater, consumption, methamphetamine-related hospitalisations, and death.

There were more than 750 overdose deaths involving amphetamine-type stimulants – primarily methamphetamine – in 2024.

That’s a rate of 2.9 deaths per 100,000 people, substantially higher than in 2021 to 2023, when it was closer to two deaths.

Evidence suggests Australia continues to have one of the highest recorded rates of methamphetamine use in the world.

Good morning, and happy Friday. Nick Visser here to take over the blog. Let’s get to that weekend, shall we?

A crime scene has been established after a police officer was killed in a crash in Sydney’s inner west.

At 1.30am, a police car was travelling on Gibbons Street in Redfern with lights and sirens on when it crashed into a tree.

Police say the passenger – a female constable – died “instantly”, while the driver – a male constable – was taken to the Royal Prince Alfred hospital in a stable condition.

In a statement, NSW’s opposition leader Kellie Sloane said she was “heartbroken”, saying the woman was “out working while most of us were asleep, protecting the community”.

double quotation markOur police put themselves in harm’s way every day to protect us. Today, we stand with them as they mourn one of their own.

Anyone with information about the incident – including dashcam footage – is urged to contact Crime Stoppers.

Australia’s gen Z are the generation most willing to cut their spending way back to afford a home, according to Cotality data reported by AAP.

The figures show more than 75% of all Australians were curbing their outgoings in pursuit of property, meaning we are more likely to do so than our Canadian, US and UK peers (for whom the figures sat below 70%).

Levels of discretionary spending, like eating out, owning a car, and even moving from the family home into a share house, have dropped among young adults in recent years.

But it wasn’t just first-time buyers making significant financial sacrifices to climb the ladder. Millennials – the largest buyer cohort in the world – are readily forgoing small luxuries to afford homes large enough for their families.

Prospective buyers were selling their second car or putting off holidays while their children were young, Capital Buyers Agency owner Claire Corby said.

double quotation markFor many, it’s around delaying things like going away, or reducing things like dinners out. People are leaving where they want to live and buying in cheaper markets.

Most Australians would not be persuaded to participate in the housing market until mortgage interest rates hit a 4.9% average, the data revealed.

The average rate for an owner-occupier in August 2026 was 6.3%, meaning the market is likely to stay quiet for some time and allowing bold buyers to swoop in.

double quotation markPeople are being conservative and cautious.

The opposition’s defence spokesperson, James Paterson, has questioned the timing of the prime minister’s announcement that an AI agent hacked Medicare.

Paterson made the claim on the ABC’s 7.30 program last night after Anthony Albanese publicly disclosed that an AI agent developed by OpenAI hacked Medicare in June and that the tech giant only notified the government earlier this month using an email sent to a “public mailbox”.

Paterson told 7.30 he believed Albanese had chosen to make the announcement at the UN summit in New York, as part of his effort to stand up to “big tech” on AI.

double quotation markThe government has questions to answer about when they knew and … why the prime minister decided to disclose it in the way he did in the place he did at the time he did. But in terms of the nature of the potential of actual security breach this is the bottom end of the spectrum of seriousness.

I don’t think it was a coincidence. I think it neatly dove-tailed with the political agenda the prime minister has in New York City.

Paterson said he didn’t consider the breach to be overly serious because the data the AI agent accessed was made freely available to researchers and academics studying the health system, and was not personal or private in nature.

He said the breach was cause for “being alert but not alarmed”.

Nevertheless, he said Australians were “entitled to demand explanations and contrition” and to want high levels of confidence when entering into agreements with big tech companies such as OpenAI.

Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it’ll be Nick Visser with the main action.

title: Mary Peltola’s campaign says reports of her using slurs and shoving staffer are exaggerated
excerpt:
Alaska Democratic nominee in pivotal Senate race ‘struggled to deal with her grief’ after death of husband and mother, spokesperson said

Mary Peltola’s campaign on Thursday downplayed a report that t...
body_text:
Alaska Democratic nominee in pivotal Senate race ‘struggled to deal with her grief’ after death of husband and mother, spokesperson said

Mary Peltola’s campaign on Thursday downplayed a report that the Democratic nominee in Alaska’s pivotal Senate race shoved a staffer and used slurs, saying the article exaggerated her behavior, but acknowledging she struggled following the deaths of her husband and mother.

The New York Times article published on Wednesday is based on text messages and interviews with nine former employees of Peltola, who served in the House of Representatives from 2022 till the beginning of last year and is now set to face Republican senator Dan Sullivan in the 3 November midterm elections.

In a statement, Harry Child, a spokesperson for Peltola’s campaign, said her behavior was affected by the stress of working in the House together with the death of her husband in a 2023 plane crash as well as her mother around the same time.

“At the time of their passing, Mary was parenting kids through their own grief, serving full-time in the US House of Representatives thousands of miles from home, and running a competitive re-election campaign – all while shouldering the enormous burden of grief,” Child said.

“Like any person who has gone through multiple personal tragedies in the span of a few months, Mary sometimes struggled to deal with her grief. But she treats her staff with respect and care, and she maintains close positive relationships with her staff spanning her nearly 30 years in public service.”

He added that “exaggerating and outright lying about moments from the hardest period of her life, and falsely presenting them as a pattern of behavior, is wrong”.

The contest between the two-term senator Sullivan, and Peltola, who lost re-election to the House in 2024, is seen as crucial to Democrats’s hopes of retaking the Senate in the midterms. Democrats must win at least four seats to gain a majority in the chamber, and have named Alaska as a top priority, in addition to Maine, North Carolina and Ohio.

Sullivan called the behavior reported by the Times “sad” and “disturbing”.

“Young Alaskans went through a lot of abuse and I’m sure there’s a hell of a lot more than was just reported in that story,” he told reporters at the US Capitol.

Other former aides to Peltola who spoke to the Times stood by her conduct.

“Mary Peltola is one of the finest human beings that I’ve ever worked for,” said Paul Horner, Peltola’s finance director in 2022, when she won both a special election to represent Alaska in the House and then a general election that year.

Tyson Fick, a special assistant who had advised Peltola on fishing policy during her time in the House, called her “awesome and demanding”, but acknowledged she occasionally “raised her voice”.

He said Peltola was dealing with grief during her time in Congress, and noted since she had previously worked on a commercial fishing boat, staffers who are not familiar with how people act in environments like that may have been misinterpreting her demeanor, the Times reported.

title: Trump officials ask supreme court to allow third-country deportations
excerpt:
Attorney general Todd Blanche requests that justices overturn lower court ruling that halted such removals

The Trump administration has asked the US supreme court to allow it to deport immigrants to ...
body_text:
Attorney general Todd Blanche requests that justices overturn lower court ruling that halted such removals

The Trump administration has asked the US supreme court to allow it to deport immigrants to countries other than their own, the latest effort to seek approval for a controversial policy that fulfils Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda.

Todd Blanche, the US attorney general, said on Thursday morning that the Department of Justice would ask the conservative-majority supreme court for help, nearly a week after a lower court judge rejected the policy.

“Without even allowing the government ⁠a chance to respond, and in the dark of night, a federal appeals court blocked us from ⁠conducting all third-country removals of illegal aliens, an entirely legal ​and invaluable tool to ‌stem the tide ‌of illegal immigration,” Blanche wrote on X.

The government filed its request by Thursday afternoon.

Blanche added: “We will ‌immediately seek relief from the supreme court, which previously granted a stay in this very same case.”

Administration officials have entered into a series of agreements with other countries that have allowed them to deport more than 25,000 ‌migrants to at least 29 third countries. In many cases, that is Mexico, according to Third Country Deportation ​Watch, a project run by Refugees International and Human Rights First.

Other immigrants have been sent to countries in Latin America, Central Asia, the Caribbean and Africa.

In some cases, US officials have deported migrants to countries considered dangerous and high risk, including the Central African Republic, which is grappling with unrest and terrorism due to political and militia instability and South Sudan, where a humanitarian crisis has been unfolding because of political and economic collapse.

Last week, a three-judge panel on the US federal appeals court in Boston rejected the Trump administration’s third-country deportation policy, upholding a lower ​court decision that declared ​the Department of Homeland ​Security’s (DHS) policy unlawful.

The ruling came in a class-action lawsuit ‌filed by migrants subject ​to ​deportation orders that has become a key test of what due-process protections the government must provide before removing people to countries with which they have no connection.

Human rights advocates have criticized the administration’s policy as “machiavellian” and said immigrants “find themselves in an extremely precarious and stressful situation” being sent to a country other than their own.

James Percival, the general counsel for DHS, has defended the administration’s deportations to third countries and refuted allegations of it being “cruel”.

“What is cruel is allowing criminal illegals who can’t be sent home to stay in our communities and victimize anew,” Percival wrote in an X post on Thursday.

title: Best DFS Apps and Promos 2026: Top Daily Fantasy Sites Reviewed

body_text:
Underdog logo signage is seen in the stands prior to the game between the Houston Roughnecks and the San Antonio Brahmas at the Alamodome on April 27, 2025, in San Antonio, Texas. (Darren Carroll/UFL/Getty Images)

With the legalization of sports betting across multiple states over the past few years, daily fantasy hasn’t been at the forefront quite as much. However, it hasn’t gone away by any means, and there are still plenty of great options if you love daily fantasy. Daily fantasy sports apps are abundant, and their promotions are often enough to convince new users to give them a chance. Below, we’ll break down the best DFS apps and help you decide which DFS promos are right for you.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Every site is competing for you and your money, so naturally, they all offer incentives to use their DFS app. This gives you the chance to pick and choose which app works best for you and which DFS promo makes the most sense. These offers change regularly, so check back often to see if a different DFS app or site is offering something better.

If there is money to be made, you’d better believe that any level of celebrity will try and create an avenue for themselves. Betr Picks—co-founded by Joey Levy and Jake Paul—is a fast-growing, mobile-exclusive DFS app designed around extreme simplicity and high-multiplier payout potential. Betr Picks focuses entirely on straightforward More/Less player stat entries with a vertical-swipe interface built specifically for modern sports fans.

Two No Sweat Entries, up to $200 back in bonus, plus a free pick

Betr operates exclusively through its mobile application, with no desktop web platform for placing entries. Using the app is a bit swipe-heavy, but it’s easy to navigate once you get the hang of it. It is intentionally designed without cluttered analytics, making it fast and simple for casual fans using mobile DFS apps.

Like many daily fantasy apps, Betr focuses on individual player performances and your ability to combine them successfully, such as passing yards, points scored or strikeout totals. You can group two to 10 player selections into a single card. Betr offers both flexible payouts, which can provide a partial return even if one leg misses, and max-multiplier entries, along with daily "Discounted Picks" and "Mystery Multiplier" spin features.

Users consistently highlight the app’s clean aesthetic, smooth entry creation, high potential payout multipliers and unique promo offers. Negative feedback generally stems from occasional location verification issues and withdrawal processing delays during high-volume sports weekends.

Betr Picks supports deposit options including major debit cards (Visa/Mastercard), PayPal, Venmo and direct online banking. Payout requests are generally straightforward, with standard e-wallet and bank transfers clearing in 24 to 48 hours.

Betr Picks operates legally in 33 U.S. states plus Washington, D.C. Most participating jurisdictions require players to be at least 18 years old, though select states require players to be 19 or 21.

Betr Picks feels like a little bit of a stripped-down DFS app, but there really isn’t anything missing from it. If you’re looking for major tournaments, this probably is not the app to use. This is mostly a player prop parlay builder app.

Final take: As far as pick’em options go, this is one of the better ones for you to go with. It is straightforward, easy to navigate and fun.

Underdog is one of the more popular DFS apps available. Most of its games are centered around Pick’em and Best Ball events. It is available in more than 40 states and is open to players 18 and older in most of them.

Deposit match up to $1,000. Also, play $5 in Fantasy Entries, get $50 in Fantasy Bonus Entries

Most users utilize the app, and that isn’t just due to convenience. The desktop site works, but the app is sleek, easy to use, and in just a few taps, you’ll be locked in for your first bet.

Pick’em lets you choose more or less on player stat lines and combine up to eight picks, with higher payouts based on how many picks you combine. Best Ball drafts and daily drafts are more traditional daily fantasy tournaments where you pick players and score fantasy points.

Coverage spans the major sports, including the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL and college football, making Underdog one of the more versatile daily fantasy sports apps available.

Users who provide positive feedback about the Underdog DFS app say how easy it is to draft their teams, the great promotional offers and the ability to combine sports for a bet. It isn’t all roses, though. Some users report constant crashing, bugs (such as auto-drafting players despite not being on auto-draft) and slow loading times in critical situations.

Underdog supports common payment methods such as debit cards, PayPal and online banking. Withdrawing money is generally easy, but payouts can sometimes be delayed. Typically, withdrawals are processed quickly and reach your bank within 24 hours.

Underdog is available in more than 40 states and is open to players 18 and older in most states. You can verify availability and any exceptions when registering.

Underdog is one of the easier-to-use DFS apps in the industry. It tends to set the bar for its competitors and generally offers everything you could be looking for.

Final take: If you’re interested in trying a DFS app, Underdog is one of the best DFS apps for beginners and a great place to start.

Dabble is a social-first DFS app that combines More/Less real-money pick'em entries with a social media-style activity feed. Originating in Australia before expanding rapidly across the U.S., its platform lets users follow top entry creators, share slips, and join community chat channels directly within the app.

Dabble is mobile-only. The user experience feels similar to using Pinterest or Instagram and other DFS apps. Between its "Banter" channels, live chat rooms, and a customizable feed of trending community slips, you can track game stats and jump into social discussions on the same screen.

Dabble keeps things focused with its More/Less Pick'em format. You pick higher or lower on two to eight player stat projections. Multipliers scale aggressively—starting at 3x for two picks up to an industry-leading 1,000x for eight-pick entries. If you’re not sure how to, or really like following people’s bets, its Copy Play capability allows you to browse public feeds and replicate another user's entire multi-leg slip with a single click.

Users love the community aspect, the ability to copy picks from top-performing players, generous multipliers and instant free bonus offers upon registration. Constructive feedback focuses on occasional app lag during high-volume sports hours, longer identity verification checks and withdrawal processing times taking up to 48–72 hours.

Dabble provides payment options like major debit/credit cards (Visa/Mastercard) and Apple Pay. Withdrawals are handled directly via direct bank transfer or online banking, with funds typically reaching your bank account within 1 to 3 business days.

Dabble is legal for real-money Pick’em contests in 27 U.S. states plus Washington, D.C. Players must be at least 18 years old in most states, 19 or older in Nebraska, and 21 or older in Massachusetts and Arizona.

Most people use help in the form of statistical sites or finding someone on X who is good at Daily Fantasy Sports. Dabble takes that idea and allows you to instantly copy their bets to your own portfolio. It is a cool and simple feature that helps all users.

Final take: If you enjoy social media interaction, sharing your picks or easily copying research from other daily fantasy players, Dabble is a must-try app.

It is always interesting to see how a company and website evolves. Amazon used to sell only books. Sleeper originally was a social-first platform for season-long and dynasty fantasy leagues. Now, its daily fantasy experience focuses heavily on Pick'em formats, live group chat integration, and custom multiplier payouts. It is legal in over 25 states for daily fantasy picks and over 40 states for traditional drafts.

Free $20 plus 100% first-deposit match up to $100

Sleeper was built for those on the go, offering one of the sleekest dark-mode interfaces in fantasy sports. Coupling live stat updates with integrated social feeds, it is easy to swap between your Pick'em tickets, group chats, and real-time game tracking without needing to leave the app.

The main draw for DFS players is Sleeper Picks, where you predict whether players will go higher or lower on dynamic stat projections. You can combine up to eight selections into a single entry with multipliers reaching as high as 100x. These, like other sites, are essentially legal parlays. Sleeper also features dynamic payout scaling based on individual player probabilities, as well as classic Daily Drafts for real-time snake drafting.

Users seem to enjoy Sleeper’s modern design, seamless social features, real-time news alerts and promotions. Critical feedback bashes the push notification delays during heavy traffic windows, withdrawal verification times for new accounts and sudden line shifts.

Sleeper accepts deposit methods such as major debit cards, PayPal and direct online banking through Plaid. Withdrawals are straightforward and typically processed into your linked bank account or PayPal within one to three business days. Keep in mind that some banks may block transactions with gaming or daily fantasy apps.

Sleeper’s traditional fantasy features and Daily Drafts are legal in more than 40 states. Paid Pick’em contests are available in more than 25 states, including California, Texas, Florida and Illinois. Players must be at least 18 years old in most participating states, 19 or older in Alabama and Nebraska, and 21 or older in Massachusetts. This makes Sleeper a widely available daily fantasy sports app.

Sleeper has found a way to combine the social aspect of sports with fantasy games. Most people start fantasy leagues with friends. Sleeper allows you to make new connections and do Daily Fantasy all in one place.

Final take: This is the app for trash-talkers, sports lovers and chronically online people. Sleeper is not one to be slept on.

ParlayPlay is a bit less known than others on the market, but shouldn’t be underestimated. Focusing on player-vs-house prop picks with unique twist formats, dynamic payouts and built-in entry protection, ParlayPlay is trying to make you rethink the options available to you.

$5 free entry plus 100% deposit match up to $100

The app sports a distinctive black-and-yellow theme that is intuitive to navigate. Browsing through player prop lines and building a multi-leg entry takes just a few seconds, with clear visuals indicating payout multipliers before you confirm your submission.

The cornerstone format is More/Less Pick'em, where you pick whether two to seven players will go over or under their projected stat lines. This is fewer inputs than you can do with other apps, but that’s not necessarily a bad thing. You can opt for "All-In" entries for maximum multiplier payouts, or use "Insured" entries, which still pay out if one or two selections miss. ParlayPlay also features HitPicks (predicting exact stat ranges) and weekly Free2Play contests offering real cash prizes.

Users love the platform's user-friendly layout, deposit match and insurance options on multi-leg entries. Criticism usually mentions a higher withdrawal minimum threshold ($30) compared to competitors and limited traditional draft/salary cap contest availability.

ParlayPlay accepts standard deposit methods including major debit/credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, Discover) and online bank transfers. Withdrawals are handled primarily via direct ACH bank transfer or e-Check, usually completing within 1 to 5 business days.

ParlayPlay is currently legal and available in 26 U.S. states, including California, Texas, Florida, Illinois, Georgia and North Carolina, plus Washington, D.C. Players must be at least 18 years old in most states, 19 or older in Alabama and Nebraska, and 21 or older in Arizona, Iowa, Louisiana, Massachusetts and Vermont.

ParlayPlay allows users to place entries with a bit of insurance. This is a great option for new users because it gives them a little more protection if a pick misses. The DFS app is easy to use and keeps the games from becoming too complicated.

Final take: If you enjoy prop-style fantasy entries and want the safety net of payout insurance on your picks, ParlayPlay is definitely worth adding to your phone.

Boom Fantasy is a prop-based daily fantasy app known for its ultra-straightforward question formats and clean, quick-entry user experience. Rather than managing complex salary caps or drafting rosters, players make quick, higher/lower or match-up choices on individual athletes' performances.

$20 minimum deposit. Play $5, Get $40 in Free entires

Boom Fantasy wants you to make your mark quickly, so their interface is very easy to use and avoids clutter. You can swipe through slates to pick what you need and make picks in seconds.

Positive reviews praise Boom Fantasy's intuitive question-style picks, unique Head-to-Head Toss-up format and reliable promotional offers. On the flip side, some users note slower withdrawal processing times during peak sports seasons and occasional app lag when submitting last-minute picks before games kickoff.

Boom Fantasy supports standard deposit options, including Visa, Mastercard and direct online banking options. Withdrawals are typically processed via ACH bank transfer or PayPal, taking between 2 to 5 business days to clear, depending on your financial institution.

Boom Fantasy is legal for real-money entries in more than 25 states plus Washington, D.C. Players must be at least 18 years old in most eligible jurisdictions, 19 or older in Alabama and Nebraska, and 21 or older in Massachusetts.

If you’re into sports betting at all, Boom Fantasy options will feel very similar. You’re essentially making player prop bets into a parlay. The toss-ups are nice because you can do either or options. The long shots are also like creating a same-game parlay on an individual player.

Final take: If you prefer question-based pick'em games over salary-cap drafts, Boom Fantasy is an engaging, easy-to-use option for your daily fantasy lineup.

body_text:
Ms. Rachel doubled down on her Gaza advocacy during an interview with Ilana Glazer, criticizing "uncancellable" celebrities who have stayed silent and asking why they would not "risk something" to help save lives.

Children's YouTube star Ms. Rachel doubled down on her Gaza advocacy Thursday, criticizing "uncancellable" celebrities who have stayed silent about Palestinian children and questioning why stars with secure careers would not "risk something" to help save lives.

Accurso, whose full name is Rachel Griffin Accurso, appeared on comedian Ilana Glazer's "It's Open" podcast to directly challenge major celebrities who have avoided taking public positions on the war.

"If you are so famous, and you’re uncancellable, and you’re so famous, and you won’t even say like, ‘Kids in Gaza should have schools, people in Gaza should have hospitals.’ Like you won't say something so basic and like why can't you risk something to help save lives," Accurso said.

MS RACHEL DEFENDS HER ACTIVISM BY POINTING TO MISTER ROGERS' POLITICAL LEGACY ON CHILDREN'S TV

Ms. Rachel criticized "uncancellable" celebrities who have stayed silent on Gaza, asking why they would not "risk something" to help save lives. (Variety via Getty Images)

Accurso’s latest remarks came after Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, recently told Fox News Digital that he believed the amount of attention she devotes to Palestinian children compared to children suffering elsewhere was disproportionate.

"When 0.09% of starving children receive 90% of her attention, something is wrong," Menken said.

Elizabeth Barcohana, the California Republican Party’s Jewish engagement chair, also criticized Accurso in a statement to Fox News Digital last week after the children’s entertainer accused celebrities and leaders who had remained silent about Gaza of applying a racial double standard.

"Ms. Rachel is essentially sanitizing terrorism with false and misleading information to emotionally manipulate her very impressionable following," Barcohana said.

MS RACHEL CLAIMS 'NO ONE NEEDS A BILLION DOLLARS,' ENDORSES DEMOCRATIC PROGRESSIVES ABDUL EL-SAYED, CORI BUSH

Ms. Rachel doubled down on her Gaza advocacy during an interview with Ilana Glazer, also calling out silence surrounding children in detention, Sudan and other humanitarian crises. (Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images)

Accurso broadened her criticism beyond Gaza during the podcast to other humanitarian issues, saying she was frustrated with prominent figures who did not publicly address them.

"I am really upset that people aren't speaking out about kids in detention and aren't speaking out about Gaza and Sudan and everything," Accurso said.

The conversation began with Glazer raising rapper Mackelmore's removal from Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour following his onstage "Free Palestine" remarks. Accurso dismissed Sheeran by name before broadening her criticism.

Tour promoter Messina Touring Group said multiple venues refused to allow Macklemore to perform, while Sheeran later said the decision to remove the rapper was made by the promoter, not him. Sheeran subsequently addressed the controversy at a Philadelphia concert, condemning the Oct. 7 Hamas attacks while describing the situation in Gaza as catastrophic and unjustifiable.

FORMULA ONE DRIVER LEWIS HAMILTON TELLS MACKLEMORE HE IS ‘STANDING’ IN SOLIDARITY WITH HIM ON PALESTINE

Rapper Macklemore was recently dropped from singer Ed Sheeran's U.S. tour after Macklemore said "Free Palestine" before a performance. (Getty Images)

Macklemore later pledged $1 million in tour proceeds to Palestinian aid organizations, a donation Accurso pledged to match as she urged other wealthy celebrities to do the same.

Accurso also repeatedly characterized Israel’s conduct in Gaza as "genocide" during the Glazer interview, saying she believed using the term could help pressure the international community to act.

A U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded in June that Israeli authorities and security forces deliberately targeted Palestinian children and said their conduct amounted to genocide and other international crimes. Israel rejected the commission’s conclusions and formally challenged what it called flaws in its composition, mandate and methodology.

A separate genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel remains before the International Court of Justice. The court has issued provisional measures in the case but has not issued a final judgment on whether Israel committed genocide.

CJ Womack is an associate editor at Fox News.

CJ joined Fox News Digital's team in 2026, which highlights the vital role journalism plays in shaping politics and culture. He has years of experience analyzing and reporting on the news media.

CJ graduated from Long Beach State University in 2025 with a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science and a minor in Journalism.

title: Dolly Parton’s sisters push back on feud rumors after nephew’s legal battle with star's estate erupts
excerpt: Entertainment lawyer Jordan Matthews weighs in on the conflict involving Dolly Parton’s nephew and explains why disputes among relatives can intensify when a famous person leaves behind a valuable bra...
body_text:
Entertainment lawyer Jordan Matthews weighs in on the conflict involving Dolly Parton’s nephew and explains why disputes among relatives can intensify when a famous person leaves behind a valuable brand.

Dolly Parton’s sisters are shutting down claims of a family feud as tensions surrounding the late country legend’s legacy have spilled into court.

Nearly one month after Parton’s death, her sisters pushed back against reports of infighting within the family, insisting they remain united as a separate legal dispute involving the singer’s longtime manager and nephew resulted in a temporary restraining order.

"I’ll say this and this only: there is no feud within our family," Freida Parton shared Wednesday on Instagram. "No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate. We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other. I love you all!!"

DOLLY PARTON’S SISTER REVEALS ‘LAST THING’ COUNTRY LEGEND ASKED OF HER BEFORE DEATH

Dolly Parton’s sisters, Freida Parton and Stella Parton, pushed back against reports of a family feud following the singer's death. (Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection)

Parton's sister Stella echoed Freida's message, emphasizing that the family remains united as it continues to navigate its grief.

"It has been a comfort to experience such an outpouring of love on [Dolly's] behalf as we grieve her passing," Stella posted Thursday on Instagram. "We are also grieving the loss of our brother Denver who passed less than a month before her. All families have the same struggles since we are all living in this world having a human experience!"

"We are still intact and moving forward because our children and grandchildren look to us for strength and guidance during this difficult time of loss and confusion for them as well," she added. "Regardless of what you may have seen on different news outlets, we are all doing what you would be doing under the same circumstances, we are living our lives one day at a time and being grateful for every blessing."

Stella Parton echoed Freida Parton’s message as the family continue grieving Dolly Parton and their brother Denver Parton. (Terry Wyatt/Getty Images)

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

Parton’s legacy took a dramatic turn this week when her longtime manager sought a restraining order against the country icon’s nephew.

Danny Nozell, who runs She's Alive, LLC, an entity Parton created to oversee her business interests, filed for the restraining order on behalf of She's Alive against Bryan Seaver and Seaver's private security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, in Nashville, according to The Associated Press.

A Tennessee judge granted the temporary restraining order Wednesday, citing a pattern of alleged threats and demands for payment, along with Seaver’s "claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate." The order called the communications "concerning" and specifically pointed to an alleged threat to use force.

Dolly Parton's longtime manager filed a restraining order on behalf of She's Alive against the singer's nephew on Tuesday. (BRIDGET BENNETT/AFP via Getty Images)

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Nozell and She's Alive accused Seaver of sending increasingly threatening messages in the weeks leading up to their request for a temporary restraining order. The filing came after She’s Alive fired Seaver over his alleged "terrorizing conduct."

Court documents obtained by The Associated Press show text messages and emails allegedly sent by Seaver.

In one message written Sept. 1 and included in the court documents, Seaver said, "I’m going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s brand partnerships and telling the violations these people have done on us. It’s going to be great. Or f---ing pay me."

WATCH: DOLLY PARTON'S BRAND MAY FUEL HIGH-STAKES ESTATE FIGHT INVOLVING HER NEPHEW, LAWYER SAYS

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

A Tennessee judge granted the temporary restraining order against Bryan Seaver after Dolly Parton’s longtime manager, Danny Nozell, accused Bryan Seaver of making threatening statements. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

Seaver pushed back against the allegations in a statement shared with TMZ. He said the messages had been taken out of context to make them appear threatening.

Seaver's company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, had provided Parton’s security detail throughout her career. Parton chose Seaver to publicly announce her death. The singer-songwriter died Aug. 25.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: What's on the menu for Trump's state dinner with China's Xi? One American staple is notably missing
excerpt:
Chinese President Xi Jinping participates in a high-profile summit with President Donald Trump as Gen. Jack Keane analyzes rising U.S.-China-Iran tensions during 'America's Newsroom.'

President Donal...
body_text:
Chinese President Xi Jinping participates in a high-profile summit with President Donald Trump as Gen. Jack Keane analyzes rising U.S.-China-Iran tensions during 'America's Newsroom.'

President Donald Trump, despite his wealth, isn't exactly known for his refined palette.

But Thursday's state dinner with Chinese President Xi Jinping will be an elegant affair, and a far cry from the 47th president's notorious McDonald's order of two Big Macs, two Filet-O-Fish sandwiches and a large chocolate shake. The swanky event will be quite the opposite.

Conspicuously missing from the menu, however, is an American dining staple — red meat.

In fact, no meat will be served at all. Instead, the dinner is exclusively a pescatarian affair.

President Donald Trump is pictured at a dinner with donors in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 15, 2025. Trump is remodeling the White House and plans to build a massive ballroom for hosting official receptions, one of the largest projects at the executive mansion in over a century. (Photo by ANDREW CABALLERO-REYNOLDS/AFP via Getty Images)

TRUMP-XI SUMMIT COULD HOLD KEY TO LOWER GAS PRICES, GOP CHAIRMAN SAYS

The menu for the event, provided to Fox News Digital by First Lady Melania Trump's office, says the first course consists of yellow squash velouté, wild mushroom fricassée, crispy pancetta and scallion oil.

"The first course offers a refined and silky-smooth velouté made of sweet yellow squash," the menu states. "This course is gently blended to highlight its delicate seasonal flavors of earthy wild mushrooms, sautéed with fresh herbs. Together, these ingredients create a rich fricassee, complemented by crispy pancetta for a savory and smoky contrast. A finishing drizzle of scallion oil adds vibrance and a subtle allium brightness to the dish."

Homemade caramel vanilla ice cream with frozen raspberries sits in a ceramic bowl on a white marble table with flowers in the background. (Natasha Breen/REDA/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

TRUMP HOSTS KING CHARLES, QUEEN CAMILLA AT WHITE HOUSE STATE DINNER: FASHION, FOOD AND A STANDOUT GIFT

Served next is a sesame crusted sea bass with braised bok choi, roasted garden eggplant and a French green herb sauce.

"The second course is prepared delicately with fresh seabass and coated in toasted sesame seeds," according to the menu.

"This combination creates a fragrant nutty crust while keeping the fish tender. The fish is served with crisp baby bok choy and roasted garden eggplant, creating lightly caramelized flavors. The dish is finished with a vibrant sauce verte of fresh herbs, which add brightness, acidity, and a garden character."

The two heads of state and their guests will enjoy vanilla crémeux and White House honey iced cream, walnut frangipane and sour cherry confit for their final course.

President Donald Trump speaks with a Doordash delivery worker after she delivered McDonald's at the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, D.C., on April 13, 2026. (Brendan SMIALOWSKI / AFP via Getty Images)

DAUGHTER OF CHINESE UYGHUR PRISONER MAKES EMOTIONAL PLEA TO TRUMP DURING SPOTLIGHT XI SUMMIT

"The dessert course is a smooth vanilla crémeux with a vibrant sour cherry confit center, set a top a rich walnut frangipane," the menu says. "The dessert’s fruit shaped form is complimented by a delicate ice cream made with harvested White House honey."

The First Lady unveiled a beehive on the White House South Lawn earlier this year.

Famous American tenor Christopher Macchio, who was featured at the Republican National Convention in Dallas a few weeks ago, will entertain for the evening, along with military musicians from the Army and the Marine Corps.

President Donald Trump is joined by opera singer Christopher Macchio on stage at the conclusion of the second day of the 2026 Republican National Convention at the American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas, on Sept. 10, 2026. (Andrew Harnik/Getty Images)

"The décor for the evening is an expression of warmth and celebration and draws on the color red’s longstanding cultural significance throughout Chinese history," the First Lady's memo says, and will feature "urns overflowing with red blossoms and tables covered by red linen with dahlias and ranunculus."

After the dinner, both presidents are expected to retire for the evening.

Friday, Trump will take Xi on an expedition to the National Archives before the communist leader departs the United States mid-afternoon.

Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Dale Earnhardt once broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm
excerpt: NASCAR driver Chase Briscoe joins OutKick OutDoors to explain how he developed a love for hunting and the outdoors, how his young son Brooks got involved, and why getting his kids away from screens an...
body_text:
NASCAR driver Chase Briscoe joins OutKick OutDoors to explain how he developed a love for hunting and the outdoors, how his young son Brooks got involved, and why getting his kids away from screens and outside matters to him.

Dale Earnhardt wasn't called "The Intimidator" for nothing. But as it turns out, the seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion didn't reserve all that intimidation for the racetrack.

Just ask the guy who decided to sneak onto his property and shoot one of his deer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

During Wednesday's episode of "The Dale Jr. Download," Dale Earnhardt Jr. recalled the time his dad broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Dale Earnhardt before the start of a NASCAR Cup race at Charlotte Motor Speedway in 1992. (ISC Images & Archives via Getty Images)

And while Earnhardt Sr. certainly wasn't afraid of a confrontation on the track, his son said he couldn't recall his dad ever getting into an actual fight with another driver.

The deer incident, though… that was a different story.

According to Dale Jr., the whole thing started back in 1993 when a man working on a tractor on Earnhardt's property spotted some deer.

Later that afternoon, the man went to a bar with a buddy and started telling him about the animals he'd seen. And, as tends to happen when alcohol enters the equation, the two came up with a brilliant idea.

They'd sneak back onto Earnhardt's property and shoot themselves a deer.

"The more they drank, the braver they got," Earnhardt Jr. recalled.

So, around dark, the two men hopped the fence and made their way onto the property.

What they didn't know was that Earnhardt and his farm manager happened to be walking along a power line nearby.

The two heard a gunshot and watched as a wounded deer ran down the clearing before collapsing. Rather than immediately confronting the trespassers, Earnhardt and his farm manager hid in the tree line and waited for the men to come retrieve the animal.

CHASE BRISCOE SAYS DEER HUNTING GIVES HIM A BIGGER RUSH THAN DRIVING 200MPH IN NASCAR

And when they showed up, The Intimidator lived up to his nickname.

According to Dale Jr., his dad charged the man carrying the gun, tackled him and began punching him in the face.

He hit the guy so hard that he broke his own hand.

Dale Earnhardt and Dale Earnhardt Jr. pose for a photo on Oct. 5, 1999, in Mooresville, N.C. (Sporting News via Getty Images)

Earnhardt eventually recognized the man's voice and realized he was the same guy who had been working on his tractor earlier that day. He then held the man until police arrived.

Earnhardt wasn't upset because someone had stolen a deer he was planning to hunt himself. He just liked having the animals around.

According to his son, Earnhardt had some impressive bucks roaming his property, but he wasn't interested in shooting them. He enjoyed watching them and wanted to keep them around.

And he certainly didn't want word getting out that his farm was home to some big deer.

So when Earnhardt showed up to the 1993 NASCAR awards banquet sporting a cast on his broken hand, he made up a different explanation for the injury.

"He didn't want people to know about his deer," Dale Jr. explained. "He didn't want more people showin' up, trying to sneak into his property."

Earnhardt even had a black-and-white cast to match his tuxedo as he accepted his sixth Cup Series championship trophy.

Dale Earnhardt checks out the view from the newly completed Earnhardt Grandstand during winter testing at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Fla., two weeks before the Daytona 500. (Getty Images)

But the broken hand created another problem when the 1994 racing season rolled around.

According to Junior, his dad was told he wouldn't be allowed to compete in the Daytona 500 while wearing the cast. So Earnhardt cut it off himself.

Anyway, let that be a lesson to you. Don't go hunting on private land without permission. It just doesn't turn out well — not for you, not for the deer, and not even for the landowner who has to knock your lights out.

Love all things hunting, wildlife and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram and TikTok!

title: Netanyahu defends Israeli military as delegates walk out before UN speech
excerpt:
Watch: UN delegates walk out of Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu's speech

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has fiercely defended his country's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in ...
body_text:
Watch: UN delegates walk out of Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu's speech

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has fiercely defended his country's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly.

After dozens of delegates walked out in protest as he took to the stage, Netanyahu vowed to continue fighting: "We're going to win. We have no other choice."

In response to the walkout, he said: "If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left the hall, please do so now."

The Israeli leader also rejected accusations that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Hours earlier, in a recorded message Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN that Israeli policies - in particular the illegal expansion of Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank - threatened "the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland".

He also said it jeopardised the two-state solution, which is an internationally backed formula for peace between Israel and the Palestinians.

Abbas said that Palestinians were being subjected to "killing, destruction, starvation and attempts at displacement, as well as a genocidal war" in Gaza by the Israeli military.

The Palestinian leader was addressing the annual gathering via a video link because had been denied a US entry visa.

Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza almost a year after a ceasefire came into force

Netanyahu, who is subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes, launched scathing attacks on nations and leaders who have criticised him.

"They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism - some colonialism. And who's accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France. For God's sake, they invented the term," he said.

He went on to label Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan a "tyrant", accusing him of supporting the Palestinian armed group Hamas.

Erdogan told the UN on Tuesday that the injustices faced by those in Gaza and the West Bank "deeply offends the conscience of humanity".

New York City's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani - who had previously vowed to arrest Netanyahu but later said he did not have the authority to do so - was also criticised by the Israeli leader.

"Since you were elected mayor of this city, many Jews no longer feel safe in New York," the Israeli prime minister said.

In a statement, Mamdani's office said Netanyahu "used his speech to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitize his genocide of Palestinians".

Netanyahu also thanked US President Donald Trump for his "bold leadership", referring to the air strikes the US and Israel jointly launched against Tehran in February.

"Israel and America acted together not only to protect ourselves, but to save civilisation," he said.

A number of people protesting against Netanyahu's visit were detained in New York City. Among them were the Oscar-winning actress Susan Sarandon and Emmy-winning actress Hannah Einbinder.

Actress Susan Sarandon was among demonstrators detained near the UN

The Israeli military launched a ground offensive in the Gaza Strip after the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack against Israel, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostages.

During the Israeli military campaign more than 73,920 people have been killed in Gaza, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

Last year, the world's leading association of genocide scholars declared that Israel was committing genocide in Gaza.

A resolution passed by the International Association of Genocide Scholars (IAGS) stated that Israel's conduct meets the legal definition as laid out in the UN convention on genocide.

Israel has regularly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide and says they are justified as a means of self-defence.

On 28 February, Israel and the US started launching massive air strikes on Iran, suspecting it of secretly building a nuclear weapon - a claim denied by Tehran.

Iran retaliated by carrying out missile and drone attacks on Israel and neighbouring Gulf Arab states which host US military bases.

Netanyahu calls Macron's remarks on West Bank in UN speech 'grotesque'

Dak Prescott and Sarah Jane Ramos attend the 15th Annual NFL Honors at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco, California, on Feb. 5, 2026. (Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic)

Following the split, her reps said, "There wasn't any rockiness in the lead up, and there was no big argument or blow up. It was a mutual decision."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

That was that, end of story. Ramos is still the mother of their two children and Dak is still the quarterback of the Cowboys. Their personal drama had died down, that was until Wednesday.

Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and Sarah Jane Ramos attend an in-store event at David Yurman in Dallas, Texas, on May 16, 2024. (Getty Images for David Yurman)

title: Angel mom says blue state DAs are putting illegal immigrant criminals before public safety
excerpt:
Cheryl Minter calls for Virginia prosecutor Steve Descano’s removal after an illegal immigrant with more than 30 prior arrests was charged in her daughter Stephanie’s bus stop killing.

A Virginia mot...
body_text:
Cheryl Minter calls for Virginia prosecutor Steve Descano’s removal after an illegal immigrant with more than 30 prior arrests was charged in her daughter Stephanie’s bus stop killing.

A Virginia mother whose daughter was stabbed to death at a bus stop is fighting to oust the county's top prosecutor after learning the accused killer had been arrested more than 30 times before the attack.

"Stephanie should be alive today," Cheryl Minter wrote in a petition calling for Fairfax County Commonwealth's Attorney Steve Descano to be removed. "I had to do what no parent should ever have to. I had to bury my daughter."

Stephanie Minter, 41, was found with multiple stab wounds inside a bus stop shelter in Hybla Valley on Feb. 23, Fairfax County police said. Abdul Jalloh, 32, is charged with second-degree murder. He has not been convicted in her death.

"She was an amazingly strong woman, amazingly strong, and happy, and brought brightness and joy to so many people," Cheryl Minter told Fox News Digital.

SOROS-BACKED DA'S LAX ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION POLICIES LED TO 'PREVENTABLE' BUS STOP STABBING MURDER: COMPLAINT

Abdul Jalloh, 32, is accused of killing Stephanie Minter, 41, at a bus stop in Virginia. (Fox 5 DC)

The Department of Homeland Security says Jalloh, a Sierra Leone national who entered the U.S. illegally in 2012, had been arrested more than 30 times. His previous charges included rape, malicious wounding, assault and theft, DHS said.

SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW

"I was shocked. I mean, literally in shock," Cheryl Minter said when asked about his record. "And then this man who's killed her, just is let off like it's nothing. Like it's nothing."

In her petition, Cheryl Minter blamed Descano's decisions for what she called a preventable death. "Thirty times the system had a chance to stop him. Thirty times," she wrote. "I think about that every single day."

JORDAN GRILLS SOROS-BACKED DA DESCANO IN HEATED SPAT OVER SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICY: 'THIS IS ALMOST LAUGHABLE'

Cheryl questioned why Jalloh was released after an arrest she recalled from the winter before Stephanie's death. The details of that case and who made the release decision have not been independently confirmed.

"When you let these people back out on the streets, they're not gonna stop. Why would they stop?" she said.

Cheryl Minter also pointed to Descano's 2020 plea bargaining policy. It told prosecutors to "consider immigration consequences where possible" and weigh how the charges could affect a defendant's immigration status, WTOP reported. The outlet reported in May that the webpage detailing the policy was no longer publicly available on Descano's office website. Cheryl Minter argues that prosecutors should put public safety first.

That policy is under federal scrutiny. The Justice Department announced in May that it was investigating whether Descano's office gave defendants who are in the country illegally preferential treatment over U.S. citizens in charging decisions and plea deals. The department said it had reached no conclusions. The investigation does not establish how Jalloh's earlier cases were handled.

SOROS-BACKED PROSECUTOR SET FOR CAPITOL HILL GRILLING AS SANCTUARY POLICIES FACE RECKONING

Descano defended the policy after receiving notice of the investigation. "My policies are fair, legal, and reflect the values of my community," he wrote in a post on X.

Asked what she wants from her petition, Cheryl Minter said her priority is changing those practices in Fairfax County and beyond. She also wants Descano out of office.

SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP

Fairfax County Commonwealth's Attorney Stephen Descano, center, listens to testimony during a hearing before a House Judiciary Subcommittee. (Tom Williams/CQ via Getty Images)

"I think first and foremost is the change," she said. "Second would be, I would love to see Descano out."

Jennifer Harrison, executive director of the Victims' Rights Reform Council, helped Cheryl Minter start the Change.org petition. Cheryl Minter said she knows an online petition cannot itself remove Descano, but hopes it will drive scrutiny of his office.

Congress is also pressing Descano for answers. House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, subpoenaed him on Sept. 16 as part of an investigation into whether prosecutors give preferential treatment to criminal suspects because of their immigration status.

Rep. Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, looks on during a hearing with the House Judiciary Committee in the Rayburn House Office Building on Sept. 03, 2025 in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

Jordan set a Sept. 25 deadline after accusing Descano's office of failing to fully comply with earlier requests.

In a previous statement to Fox News Digital, Descano's office called the subpoena a "needless escalation" and accused the committee of waging a "partisan siege" against Fairfax County. It said the office had turned over more than 1,100 pages of documents, that Descano had voluntarily testified, and that it would continue to respond to legitimate inquiries while working to keep the county safe.

The office has separately said it is prosecuting Jalloh for Stephanie's murder, with a trial scheduled for January 2027, and cannot comment further on the pending case.

WATCH: SOROS PROSECUTOR’S HEARING DEVOLVES INTO ANGRY CHAOS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RAPE CASE: 'BE QUIET!'

Fairfax County police said Jalloh was arrested after an employee at a local business recognized him and called authorities the day after Stephanie Minter was killed. He was held without bond.

ICE lodged a detainer on Feb. 25, after Jalloh was in custody, asking to be notified before his release, according to DHS. The agency said it had also lodged a detainer against him in 2020 and that an immigration judge later ordered him removed to a country other than Sierra Leone.

Cheryl Minter said employees of Descano's office working on her daughter's murder case have been "wonderful with me." She said her criticism is aimed at the decisions she believes left a repeat offender free.

"I want people never to stop talking about it," she said. "I just don't want the talk to stop, and I'll do whatever to keep it going."

"Stephanie cannot speak for herself anymore. So I am," she wrote in the petition.

Fox News Digital reached out to Descano's office for comment on Cheryl Minter's allegations and petition.

Fox News Digital's Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this report.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.
